title: infra-sim design
description: A design for infra-sim: its components (nodes), the connections between them (edges), and what happens to it (scenarios).

description.description: What it is for. The first paragraph is its short blurb.

seed.description: Random seed: the same design and seed always play out the same.

accounts.description: Account quotas by placement (such as aws:us-east-1): limits shared by everything in that account and region. Only what you change.

^aws:.description: Account quotas of Amazon Web Services in one region: only the ones you change.

lambdaConcurrency.title: Lambda concurrent executions
lambdaConcurrency.description: Shared by every function in this region. At least 100 always stays unreserved, and each unit allows 10 synchronous requests a second. In executions. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

apiGatewayRate.title: API Gateway request rate
apiGatewayRate.description: Steady-state rate shared by every API in this region, REST, HTTP and WebSocket alike. The burst (5,000) is fixed by AWS. In req/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

apiGatewayIntegrationTimeout.title: API Gateway maximum integration timeout
apiGatewayIntegrationTimeout.description: The longest integration timeout a REST API may be given. AWS raises it for Regional and private REST APIs only (edge-optimized APIs stay at 29 s, HTTP APIs at 30 s), and says a raise may cost some of the regional throttle quota. The 5 minute ceiling here is an assumption: AWS publishes no upper bound. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

snsPublishRate.title: SNS publish rate (standard)
snsPublishRate.description: Messages published per second across every standard topic in this region (Publish and PublishBatch together, counting each message of a batch). In msg/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

snsFifoPublishRate.title: SNS publish rate (FIFO)
snsFifoPublishRate.description: Messages published per second across every FIFO topic in this region. A topic in Topic throughput scope is further limited to 3,000 a second, and every message group to 300. In msg/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

snsStandardTopics.title: SNS standard topics
snsStandardTopics.description: Standard topics one account may have in a region. In topics. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

snsFifoTopics.title: SNS FIFO topics
snsFifoTopics.description: FIFO topics one account may have in a region. In topics. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

sqsFifoHighThroughput.title: SQS FIFO high-throughput limit
sqsFifoHighThroughput.description: Per queue, non-batched requests per second when high-throughput mode is on. Batched is ten times this. In req/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

kinesisShards.title: Kinesis shards per region
kinesisShards.description: Shards every stream in this region may hold together, on-demand streams included. Resharding creates short-lived shards that count too. In shards. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

kinesisOnDemandStreams.title: Kinesis on-demand streams
kinesisOnDemandStreams.description: Streams in on-demand mode an account may have. Provisioned streams have no such limit. In streams. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

kinesisOnDemandWriteMBps.title: Kinesis on-demand write ceiling
kinesisOnDemandWriteMBps.description: The most one on-demand stream scales to (reads get twice this). 10 GB/s in N. Virginia, Oregon and Ireland; 200 MB/s elsewhere, raisable to 10 GB/s on request. In MB/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

firehoseDirectPutMiBps.title: Firehose Direct PUT throughput
firehoseDirectPutMiBps.description: Per Firehose stream, with records/s and requests/s raised in proportion (here 500,000 records/s and 2,000 requests/s at the default). Streams reading a Kinesis stream aren't limited by it. In MiB/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

firehoseStreams.title: Firehose streams per region
firehoseStreams.description: In streams. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

dynamodbTableReadUnits.title: DynamoDB per-table read units
dynamodbTableReadUnits.description: The most read units a table, or any one of its indexes, can have provisioned, or use on-demand. In units/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

dynamodbTableWriteUnits.title: DynamoDB per-table write units
dynamodbTableWriteUnits.description: In units/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

dynamodbAccountReadUnits.title: DynamoDB account read units
dynamodbAccountReadUnits.description: Provisioned read capacity summed across all tables and indexes in this region. On-demand tables don't count. In units/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

dynamodbAccountWriteUnits.title: DynamoDB account write units
dynamodbAccountWriteUnits.description: In units/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

dynamodbTables.title: DynamoDB tables per region
dynamodbTables.description: AWS raises this to 10,000 through your account team; beyond that it recommends more accounts. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

dynamodbIndexesPerTable.title: DynamoDB global secondary indexes per table
dynamodbIndexesPerTable.description: The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

opensearchDomains.title: OpenSearch domains per region
opensearchDomains.description: In domains. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

opensearchInstancesPerDomain.title: OpenSearch instances per domain
opensearchInstancesPerDomain.description: AWS raises it to at most 1,002 (T2 and T3 domains stay at 10). The developer guide lists 80 as the default for most instance families; this is the Service Quotas default from the General Reference. In instances. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

elasticacheNodesPerRegion.title: ElastiCache nodes per region
elasticacheNodesPerRegion.description: Non-reserved nodes across every cluster in the region. Checked against the design, not enforced while running. In nodes. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

elasticacheNodesPerCluster.title: ElastiCache nodes per cluster (cluster mode)
elasticacheNodesPerCluster.description: Nodes in one Valkey or Redis OSS cluster with cluster mode on: shards x (1 + replicas). A cluster asking for more runs with as many shards as fit. Raisable to 500. In nodes. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

elasticacheMemcachedNodesPerCluster.title: ElastiCache Memcached nodes per cluster
elasticacheMemcachedNodesPerCluster.description: Nodes in one Memcached cluster. A cluster asking for more runs with as many as the quota allows. In nodes. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

elasticacheServerlessCachesPerRegion.title: ElastiCache serverless caches per region
elasticacheServerlessCachesPerRegion.description: Checked against the design, not enforced while running. In caches. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

rdsInstances.title: RDS DB instances
rdsInstances.description: RDS and Aurora DB instances together: each database's writer, its readers or read replicas, and a Multi-AZ DB cluster's two standbys. (A Multi-AZ DB instance's standby is not counted here.) The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

rdsClusters.title: RDS Aurora DB clusters
rdsClusters.description: Aurora clusters in this region. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

rdsReadReplicas.title: RDS read replicas per primary
rdsReadReplicas.description: Read replicas of one RDS primary. Aurora's 15 replicas per cluster can't be adjusted. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

rdsProxies.title: RDS Proxies
rdsProxies.description: The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

rdsStorage.title: RDS total storage
rdsStorage.description: Storage allocated to every RDS DB instance together (read replicas included). Aurora doesn't count. In GB. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

s3GeneralPurposeBuckets.title: S3 general purpose buckets
s3GeneralPurposeBuckets.description: General purpose buckets an account can own. It is an account-wide quota; the check here only counts the buckets of this design in one region. In buckets. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

s3DirectoryBuckets.title: S3 directory buckets
s3DirectoryBuckets.description: S3 Express One Zone directory buckets an account can own. In buckets. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

s3ReplicationTransferRate.title: S3 Replication Time Control transfer rate
s3ReplicationTransferRate.description: The most data a region's buckets can replicate with S3 RTC, together. Beyond it the 15-minute SLA stops applying and replicas queue. In Gb/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

route53HealthChecks.title: Route 53 active health checks
route53HealthChecks.description: Health checks the account may have. AWS refuses to create one past it, so a record that asks for one when none are left has no health check and is always treated as healthy. In health checks. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

cloudfrontRequestRate.title: CloudFront requests per distribution
cloudfrontRequestRate.description: Requests per second one distribution accepts. AWS publishes no burst size or response for going over; the model gives a one second bucket and answers 503, which AWS documents as 'capacity exceeded' at an edge location. In req/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

cloudfrontDataTransferRate.title: CloudFront data transfer per distribution
cloudfrontDataTransferRate.description: Bytes per second one distribution may send, in gigabits a second. In Gbps. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

cloudfrontLambdaEdgeRate.title: Lambda@Edge requests per region
cloudfrontLambdaEdgeRate.description: Lambda@Edge invocations per second in each AWS Region, shared by every distribution of the account. Over it, the viewer gets a 503. In req/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

sesSandbox.title: SES sandbox
sesSandbox.description: New SES accounts start in the sandbox, per region: mail goes only to verified addresses and the mailbox simulator, at the sandbox quota and rate. Off here (production access) because designs usually model a live system; turn it on to see what a new account hits.

sesSandboxDailyQuota.title: SES daily quota (sandbox)
sesSandboxDailyQuota.description: Recipients the account may send in a rolling 24 hours while it is in the sandbox. In recipients/24 h. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

sesSandboxSendingRate.title: SES sending rate (sandbox)
sesSandboxSendingRate.description: Recipients per second the account may send while it is in the sandbox. In recipients/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

sesDailyQuota.title: SES daily quota (production)
sesDailyQuota.description: Recipients the account may send in a rolling 24 hours once out of the sandbox. AWS publishes no default (it depends on your use case and sending history); 50,000 is an assumption. In recipients/24 h. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

sesSendingRate.title: SES sending rate (production)
sesSendingRate.description: Recipients per second once out of the sandbox. AWS publishes no default; 14 per second is an assumption. Short bursts above it are allowed (the bucket holds one second's worth, an assumption). In recipients/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

eventBridgePutEventsRate.title: EventBridge PutEvents rate
eventBridgePutEventsRate.description: PutEvents requests per second across every event bus in this region. AWS's quota counts requests, so a request of 10 entries uses one. Requests over it are throttled (ThrottlingException). In req/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

eventBridgeInvocationRate.title: EventBridge invocation rate
eventBridgeInvocationRate.description: Target invocations per second across every rule in this region: one per target per matched event. Invocations over it are delayed, not refused. In inv/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

eventBridgeRulesPerBus.title: EventBridge rules per bus
eventBridgeRulesPerBus.description: Rules one event bus may have. Rules wired past it are left out (AWS refuses to create them). In rules. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

eventBridgeBuses.title: EventBridge event buses
eventBridgeBuses.description: Event buses one account may have in this region. In buses. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

schedulerInvocationRate.title: Scheduler invocation rate
schedulerInvocationRate.description: Target invocations per second across every schedule in this region. Invocations over it are delayed, not refused (InvocationThrottleCount). In inv/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

schedulerSchedules.title: Scheduler schedules
schedulerSchedules.description: Schedules one account may have in this region. In schedules. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

sfnStartExecutionBurst.title: Step Functions StartExecution bucket (Standard)
sfnStartExecutionBurst.description: How many Standard executions can be started at once from a full bucket. Past it, StartExecution is throttled (ThrottlingException). In calls. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

sfnStartExecutionRate.title: Step Functions StartExecution refill (Standard)
sfnStartExecutionRate.description: Standard executions started per second, sustained, across every state machine in this region. In calls/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

sfnStateTransitionBurst.title: Step Functions state transition bucket (Standard)
sfnStateTransitionBurst.description: State transitions (states entered, and retries) a Standard workflow can make at once from a full bucket. Past it, executions are slowed down, not failed: each transition waits for a token (CloudWatch's ExecutionThrottled). In transitions. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

sfnStateTransitionRate.title: Step Functions state transition refill (Standard)
sfnStateTransitionRate.description: State transitions per second, sustained, across every Standard execution in this region. Express workflows have no such limit. In transitions/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

sfnExpressStartBurst.title: Step Functions StartExecution bucket (Express)
sfnExpressStartBurst.description: Asynchronous Express executions that can be started at once from a full bucket. Synchronous ones (StartSyncExecution) don't count against it. In calls. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

sfnExpressStartRate.title: Step Functions StartExecution refill (Express)
sfnExpressStartRate.description: Asynchronous Express executions started per second, sustained, across every Express state machine in this region. In calls/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

sfnOpenExecutions.title: Step Functions open executions (Standard)
sfnOpenExecutions.description: Standard executions that may be running at once in this region. Past it, StartExecution fails with ExecutionLimitExceeded. Express workflows don't count. In executions. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

vpcPerRegion.title: VPCs per Region
vpcPerRegion.description: How many VPC boxes the account can have in this Region. AWS says it can be raised to hundreds; the upper bound here is only for the slider. In VPCs. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

vpcSubnetsPerVpc.title: Subnets per VPC
vpcSubnetsPerVpc.description: The most subnets one VPC can hold. Checked against a VPC's subnet plan. In subnets. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

vpcNatGatewaysPerAz.title: NAT gateways per Availability Zone
vpcNatGatewaysPerAz.description: Counted per zone across every VPC in the account. Only pending, active and deleting gateways count. In NAT gateways. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

vpcNatAddressesPerGateway.title: Elastic IP addresses per public NAT gateway
vpcNatAddressesPerGateway.description: Each address adds 55,000 simultaneous connections to a destination. AWS allows up to 8 on request. In addresses. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

vpcElasticIpsPerRegion.title: Elastic IP addresses per Region
vpcElasticIpsPerRegion.description: A public NAT gateway holds at least one. The account's other Elastic IPs (EC2 instances) are not simulated. In addresses. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

vpcGatewayEndpointsPerRegion.title: Gateway endpoints per Region
vpcGatewayEndpointsPerRegion.description: S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints across every VPC in the Region. One VPC can hold at most 255. In endpoints. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

vpcInterfaceEndpointsPerVpc.title: Interface endpoints per VPC
vpcInterfaceEndpointsPerVpc.description: A combined quota for interface endpoints and Gateway Load Balancer endpoints. In endpoints. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

wafWebAcls.title: WAF web ACLs (regional)
wafWebAcls.description: Regional web ACLs (for ALBs, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito, App Runner, Verified Access) the account may have in this Region. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

wafCloudFrontWebAcls.title: WAF web ACLs (CloudFront)
wafCloudFrontWebAcls.description: Web ACLs for CloudFront distributions the account may have. They are global and created in us-east-1, so this counts only there. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

ec2OnDemandStandardVcpus.title: EC2 running On-Demand Standard vCPUs
ec2OnDemandStandardVcpus.description: Running On-Demand Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) instances: the vCPUs of every running On-Demand instance of those families in the region. A launch past it fails and the group retries. Stopped and pending instances don't count. In vCPUs. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

ec2SpotStandardVcpus.title: EC2 Spot Standard vCPUs
ec2SpotStandardVcpus.description: All Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instance Requests: the vCPUs of running and requested Spot Instances in the region. A Spot launch past it fails and the group retries. In vCPUs. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

ec2AutoScalingGroups.title: EC2 Auto Scaling groups
ec2AutoScalingGroups.description: Auto Scaling groups per region. Checked by the design audit. In groups. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

elbApplicationLoadBalancers.title: Application Load Balancers
elbApplicationLoadBalancers.description: Application Load Balancers the account may have in this Region. In load balancers. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

elbNetworkLoadBalancers.title: Network Load Balancers
elbNetworkLoadBalancers.description: Network Load Balancers the account may have in this Region. In load balancers. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

elbReservedAlbLcus.title: Reserved ALB capacity units
elbReservedAlbLcus.description: LCUs the Application Load Balancers in this Region may reserve between them. 0 by default: ask AWS to raise it before reserving capacity for an event. In LCU. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

fargateOnDemandVcpus.title: Fargate On-Demand vCPUs
fargateOnDemandVcpus.description: The vCPUs of every Fargate (On-Demand) task running in the region, together. A task past it waits in PROVISIONING and is tried again. 6 is the default; established accounts usually have far more. In vCPUs. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

fargateSpotVcpus.title: Fargate Spot vCPUs
fargateSpotVcpus.description: The vCPUs of every Fargate Spot task running in the region. Spot tasks past it wait; Fargate never moves them to On-Demand. In vCPUs. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

fargateLaunchRate.title: Fargate task launch rate
fargateLaunchRate.description: Fargate tasks launched per second in the region, sustained (a token bucket refilled at this rate). Launches past it wait and are tried again. 5 in newer Regions. In tasks/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

fargateLaunchBurst.title: Fargate task launch burst
fargateLaunchBurst.description: Fargate tasks that can be launched at once before the rate applies. 25 in newer Regions. In tasks. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

edges.description: The connections, by id (such as web.out->api).

controllers.description: Loops that change nodes while the design runs, by id.

scenarios.description: What happens to the design, by id. Play one with infra-sim run <design> --scenario <id>, or in the app's Scenario tab.

common.client.settings.description: Settings of Clients: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

arrival.title: Arrival
arrival.description: Poisson: random, bursty arrivals like real users. Constant: evenly spaced. One of: poisson (Poisson), constant (Constant).

payload.title: Request size
payload.description: Size of each request. Services enforce their own payload limits against it. In KB.

hotKeys.title: Hot key share
hotKeys.description: Fraction of requests that use the same partition key. Stores and streams partition by key, so a hot key can overload one partition while the rest sit idle. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

messageGroups.title: FIFO message groups
messageGroups.description: Spread requests across this many message groups (0 for none). FIFO queues process one message per group at a time.

invocation.title: Invocation
invocation.description: How requests invoke what they call. Lambda queues async invocations and retries them; sync ones are answered or throttled at once. One of: sync (Sync), async (Async).

records.title: Records per request
records.description: How many records one request carries: 1 for a plain call, more for a batch API (a Kinesis PutRecords, an OpenSearch bulk, EventBridge PutEvents). Services count records where AWS does. The request size is the whole batch's. In records.

common.http-endpoint.settings.description: Settings of HTTP endpoint: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

latency.title: Response time
latency.description: How long the receiver takes to answer, once the request arrives.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

errorRate.title: Error rate
errorRate.description: Fraction of requests answered with a 5xx. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

rateLimit.title: Rate limit
rateLimit.description: Requests per second before it answers 429. 0 for no limit. In req/s.

burst.title: Rate limit burst
burst.description: Requests allowed above the steady rate at once. 0 allows as many as one second's worth.

maxConcurrency.title: Max concurrent requests
maxConcurrency.description: Beyond this it answers 503 at once. 0 for no limit. In requests.

maxPayload.title: Max request size
maxPayload.description: Larger requests are refused with 413. 0 for no limit. In KB.

common.service.settings.description: Settings of Service: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

replicas.title: Replicas
replicas.description: Copies of the service running. Added ones take the start-up time to become ready; removed ones finish what they are doing. An autoscaler (a target-tracking controller) can drive this. In replicas.

concurrency.title: Requests per replica
concurrency.description: How many requests one replica works on at once: its threads, or its event loop's practical limit. In requests.

serviceTime.title: Service time
serviceTime.description: How long a request keeps a worker busy, before any downstream calls.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

queueLimit.title: Queue limit
queueLimit.description: Requests that may wait for a free worker: in one line in front of the service when it is called directly, or in front of each replica when a load balancer (a target group) picks replicas. Beyond it they are refused at once with 503. 0 refuses whenever every worker is busy. In requests.

startup.title: Start-up time
startup.description: How long a new replica takes to become ready: scheduling, pulling the image, booting, passing its readiness check. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

errorRate.title: Error rate
errorRate.description: Fraction of requests that fail after being worked on. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

fanOut.title: Downstream calls
fanOut.description: After its own work, call every output one after another, all at once, pick one by weight, or call none. One of: sequential (Sequential), parallel (Parallel), weighted (Weighted), none (None).

zones.title: Zones
zones.description: Spread the replicas evenly over this many zones of its region (the first ones: a, b, c...). A zone outage takes down the replicas there, and the service starts replacements in the other zones, then evens out again when the zone is back. 0: not spread, and no zone fault reaches it. In zones.

replaceAfter.title: Notices a lost replica after
replaceAfter.description: How long until the service notices on its own that a replica died (its zone went down) and starts another. An assumption: Kubernetes marks a node that stops reporting NotReady after 40 seconds. A target group's health checks may notice sooner. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

drain.title: Drain time
drain.description: How long a replica that is let go (scaled in, replaced) has to finish what it holds: it takes no new requests, stops as soon as it holds none, and is cut off when the time runs out. Kubernetes' default termination grace period is 30 seconds. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

common.actor.settings.description: Settings of Actors (keyed objects): only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

objects.title: Objects
objects.description: How many distinct objects the traffic is spread over. A request's partition key picks its object, so a client's hot keys are hot objects. In objects.

concurrency.title: Requests at once per object
concurrency.description: 1 is single-threaded: an object's requests run one after another, as a Durable Object's or an actor's do. Everything an object can do is bounded by this. In requests.

handlerTime.title: Handler time
handlerTime.description: How long one request keeps its object busy, before any downstream call.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

holdDuringDownstream.title: Busy while calling downstream
holdDuringDownstream.description: Keep the object busy while it waits on its downstream calls, as a Durable Object's input gate holds other requests while it waits on its storage. Off: the object takes its next request while the call is in flight.

queueLimit.title: Queue limit per object
queueLimit.description: Requests that may wait for one object. Beyond it they are refused at once (503, overloaded), as Durable Objects refuse an object whose queue is too long. In requests.

coldStart.title: Cold start
coldStart.description: Making an object that isn't in memory: starting it and loading its state. Its first requests wait for it.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

idle.title: Evicted after idle
idle.description: An object with nothing to do for this long is evicted from memory; the next request to it starts it again, cold. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

errorRate.title: Error rate
errorRate.description: Fraction of requests that fail in the handler. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

fanOut.title: Downstream calls
fanOut.description: After the handler: call every output one after another (its storage, say), all at once, pick one by weight, or call none. One of: sequential (Sequential), parallel (Parallel), weighted (Weighted), none (None).

aws.region.settings.description: Settings of Region: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

region.title: Region
region.description: One of: us-east-1 (N. Virginia (us-east-1)), us-east-2 (Ohio (us-east-2)), us-west-1 (N. California (us-west-1)), us-west-2 (Oregon (us-west-2)), ca-central-1 (Canada (Central) (ca-central-1)), ca-west-1 (Calgary (ca-west-1)), mx-central-1 (Mexico (Central) (mx-central-1)), sa-east-1 (São Paulo (sa-east-1)), eu-west-1 (Ireland (eu-west-1)), eu-west-2 (London (eu-west-2)), eu-west-3 (Paris (eu-west-3)), eu-central-1 (Frankfurt (eu-central-1)), eu-central-2 (Zurich (eu-central-2)), eu-north-1 (Stockholm (eu-north-1)), eu-south-1 (Milan (eu-south-1)), eu-south-2 (Spain (eu-south-2)), il-central-1 (Tel Aviv (il-central-1)), me-south-1 (Bahrain (me-south-1)), me-central-1 (UAE (me-central-1)), af-south-1 (Cape Town (af-south-1)), ap-south-1 (Mumbai (ap-south-1)), ap-south-2 (Hyderabad (ap-south-2)), ap-east-1 (Hong Kong (ap-east-1)), ap-east-2 (Taipei (ap-east-2)), ap-southeast-1 (Singapore (ap-southeast-1)), ap-southeast-2 (Sydney (ap-southeast-2)), ap-southeast-3 (Jakarta (ap-southeast-3)), ap-southeast-4 (Melbourne (ap-southeast-4)), ap-southeast-5 (Malaysia (ap-southeast-5)), ap-southeast-6 (New Zealand (ap-southeast-6)), ap-southeast-7 (Thailand (ap-southeast-7)), ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo (ap-northeast-1)), ap-northeast-2 (Seoul (ap-northeast-2)), ap-northeast-3 (Osaka (ap-northeast-3)).

aws.vpc.settings.description: Settings of VPC: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

cidrPrefix.title: IPv4 prefix length
cidrPrefix.description: A /16 holds 65,536 addresses, a /28 only 16. In /n. A hard limit of the provider.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Describe how the VPC is split into subnets, to check that the plan fits the address block and the subnet quota. Off leaves the VPC as a plain boundary.

availabilityZones.title: Availability Zones
availabilityZones.description: A subnet lives in one zone, so a VPC spreads over zones by having subnets in each. Checked against how many zones the Region has. In zones.

subnetsPerZone.title: Subnets per zone
subnetsPerZone.description: For example one public and one private.

prefix.title: Subnet prefix length
prefix.description: Every subnet takes this size. Five of its addresses are always reserved. In /n. A hard limit of the provider.

aws.nat-gateway.settings.description: Settings of NAT gateway: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

zone.title: Availability Zone
zone.description: A NAT gateway lives in one zone, with redundancy inside it. If that zone goes down, everything routed through it loses its way out: inject an outage on this node to see it. Counted against the NAT gateways per zone quota. One of: a (a), b (b), c (c), d (d), e (e), f (f).

addresses.title: IPv4 addresses
addresses.description: One primary and up to seven secondary. Each address supports 55,000 simultaneous connections to a destination. An account can attach 2 by default (an account quota). In addresses. A hard limit of the provider.

connectionsPerDestination.title: Connections per address and destination
connectionsPerDestination.description: Simultaneous connections one address supports to one destination (an edge leaving this gateway). The limit is 55,000: lower it to see what exhausting ports looks like with less load. In connections. A hard limit of the provider.

bandwidth.title: Bandwidth
bandwidth.description: A NAT gateway supports 5 Gbps and scales automatically up to 100 Gbps. AWS publishes no schedule for the scaling, so the simulator holds the gateway at this value: raise it to model one that has scaled. In Gbps. A hard limit of the provider.

routing.title: Destinations
routing.description: A real NAT gateway forwards whatever the client addressed. A call carries no address here, so with several destinations wired this picks one by edge weight, or calls them all. One of: weighted (Weighted), sequential (Sequential), parallel (Parallel).

latency.title: Processing latency
latency.description: Time the gateway adds to a call. AWS publishes no figure: an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

aws.vpc-endpoint.settings.description: Settings of VPC endpoint: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

type.title: Endpoint type
type.description: A gateway endpoint is a route to S3 or DynamoDB: free, no appliance in the path, same Region only. An interface endpoint is a network interface in your subnets that reaches most other AWS services over PrivateLink. One of: gateway (Gateway (S3, DynamoDB)), interface (Interface (PrivateLink)).

availabilityZones.title: Availability Zones
availabilityZones.description: Interface endpoints only: how many zones the endpoint has a network interface in. Bandwidth is per zone. In zones.

bandwidth.title: Bandwidth
bandwidth.description: Interface endpoints only. Each endpoint supports 10 Gbps per zone and scales automatically up to 100. AWS publishes no schedule for the scaling, so the simulator holds it at this value. Gateway endpoints have no published bandwidth limit. In Gbps per zone. A hard limit of the provider.

latency.title: Interface hop latency
latency.description: Time an interface endpoint adds to a call: one more network hop through its interface. AWS publishes no figure: an assumption. A gateway endpoint adds none.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

aws.apigateway.settings.description: Settings of API Gateway: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

apiType.title: Api type
apiType.description: HTTP APIs are fixed at a 30 s integration timeout and have no usage plans or response cache; REST APIs cap at 29 s unless the account quota is raised. One of: rest (REST API), http (HTTP API).

endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.description: REST endpoint type. Only Regional and private REST APIs can be given an integration timeout above 29 s; edge-optimized APIs stay at 29 s. The edge CloudFront hop is not modelled. Ignored for HTTP APIs. One of: regional (Regional), edge (Edge-optimized), private (Private).

integrationType.title: Integration type
integrationType.description: Lambda, HTTP and AWS-service integrations all look the same here: the gateway calls whatever is connected to its Integration port. MOCK answers at the gateway and calls nothing. One of: proxy (Call the connected integration), mock (MOCK (answer at the gateway)).

integrationTimeout.title: Integration timeout
integrationTimeout.description: How long the gateway waits for the backend before answering 504. The backend keeps working afterwards. The effective limit is the smaller of this and what the API type allows: 30 s for HTTP, 29 s for edge-optimized REST, the account's integration timeout quota for Regional and private REST. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

overhead.title: Gateway overhead
overhead.description: Time the gateway itself adds (CloudWatch Latency minus IntegrationLatency). AWS publishes no figure, so this is an assumption; typical values are a few to a few tens of ms.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

rate.title: Stage rate limit
rate.description: Default throttle for every method (REST) or route (HTTP) of the stage, below the account limit. With one route it is the stage's limit. 0 for none. In req/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

burst.title: Stage burst
burst.description: Bucket size for the stage limit. 0 uses the rate.

routes.title: Routes
routes.description: How many methods or routes the API has. Requests spread evenly over them by their key (a hot key lands on one), and the stage throttle is applied to each separately. With 1 the whole API shares one stage bucket. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: REST APIs only: identify clients by API key and throttle and cap each one. HTTP APIs have no usage plans, so this is ignored for them.

clients.title: API keys
clients.description: Distinct clients. Requests spread over them by key, so a hot key is one noisy client. A hard limit of the provider.

rate.title: Rate per client
rate.description: Steady rate for each API key (the plan's throttle). 0 for none. Applied before the stage and account limits. In req/s.

burst.title: Burst per client
burst.description: Bucket size per API key. 0 uses the rate.

quota.title: Quota per client
quota.description: Requests each key may make per period. 0 for none. Over it the client gets 429 until the period turns. In requests.

period.title: Period
period.description: The quota period. Windows are aligned to the start of the simulation (a month is 30 days); AWS aligns them to the calendar, so this is an assumption. One of: day (Day), week (Week), month (Month).

type.title: Type
type.description: A Lambda authorizer calls the function connected to the Authorizer port (or, if nothing is connected, is timed by the latency below). JWT, IAM and Cognito are checked inside API Gateway and cost only the latency below. One of: none (None), lambda (Lambda authorizer), jwt (JWT (HTTP APIs)), iam (IAM (SigV4)), cognito (Cognito user pool (REST)).

latency.title: Check latency
latency.description: What authorising takes when no function is connected, and what JWT, IAM and Cognito checks cost. AWS publishes no figure: an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

ttl.title: Result cache TTL
ttl.description: Lambda authorizers only. How long an allow or deny is cached per caller identity, so the function is not called again. 0 turns caching off. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

identities.title: Distinct callers
identities.description: How many different identities (tokens or header values) make requests. The authorizer result is cached per identity, so more callers means more authorizer calls.

deny.title: Denied callers
deny.description: Share of identities the authorizer refuses. They get 403 (the answer is cached like an allow). A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: REST APIs only: a stage cache in front of the integration. HTTP APIs have none, so this is ignored for them.

size.title: Size
size.description: Cache capacity. Together with the response size it decides how many entries fit; the oldest entry goes first when it is full (AWS does not publish its eviction policy). Changing it empties the cache. One of: 0.5 (0.5 GB), 1.6 (1.6 GB), 6.1 (6.1 GB), 13.5 (13.5 GB), 28.4 (28.4 GB), 58.2 (58.2 GB), 118 (118 GB), 237 (237 GB).

ttl.title: TTL
ttl.description: How long a response is cached. 0 turns caching off. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

keys.title: Distinct cache keys
keys.description: How many different responses callers ask for (distinct values of the cache key parameters). The hit ratio comes from this: few keys, high ratio. A request's key decides which one it asks for.

responseSize.title: Response size
responseSize.description: Typical size of a cached response. Responses over 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes) are never cached. In KB. A hard limit of the provider.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Which requests are cached. Enabling a stage cache caches GET only; other methods need an override. A GET is a call whose edge into the gateway has Operation: read. One of: get (GET only (AWS default)), all (Every method).

hitLatency.title: Hit latency
hitLatency.description: Time to answer from the cache, on top of the gateway overhead. AWS publishes no figure: an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

invalidate.title: Cache-Control: max-age=0
invalidate.description: Share of requests that ask for a fresh copy. They go to the integration and replace the cached entry. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

invalidation.title: Invalidation
invalidation.description: What happens to a Cache-Control: max-age=0 request. With no InvalidateCache policy any client can invalidate; with one, unauthorised requests either fail with 403 or are served from the cache. One of: allowed (Anyone may invalidate (no policy)), forbidden (Unauthorized: fail with 403), ignored (Unauthorized: ignore the header).

aws.cloudfront.settings.description: Settings of CloudFront distribution: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

objects.title: Distinct objects
objects.description: How many different objects (cache keys) the distribution serves. Requests pick one by their key, so a few objects means a high hit ratio and many objects a low one. A modelling choice.

popularitySkew.title: Popularity skew
popularitySkew.description: 1 spreads requests evenly over the objects. Higher values concentrate them on the first few (a long tail), as real traffic does: object i of N is asked for with probability proportional to its share of the key space raised to 1/skew.

objectSize.title: Object size
objectSize.description: Average response size. The bytes viewers download, what the origin sends on a miss, and what compression shrinks. In KB. A hard limit of the provider.

allowedMethods.title: Allowed methods
allowedMethods.description: Which HTTP methods the behaviour accepts. A call whose operation is write is a PUT/POST/PATCH/DELETE: it is never cached and goes straight to the origin. When only GET and HEAD are allowed, CloudFront answers a write with 403. One of: read (GET, HEAD), all (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETE).

defaultTtl.title: Default TTL
defaultTtl.description: How long an object stays cached when the origin sends no Cache-Control or Expires header. AWS's default is 86,400 s. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

minTtl.title: Minimum TTL
minTtl.description: Objects stay cached at least this long, even when the origin says no-store or a shorter max-age. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

maxTtl.title: Maximum TTL
maxTtl.description: Caps a max-age or s-maxage the origin sends. AWS's default is 31,536,000 s (one year). A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

originCacheControl.title: Origin cache control
originCacheControl.description: What the origin tells CloudFront about every object. Together with the TTLs above it fixes how long an object is cached (see the table in the README). One of: none (No Cache-Control (use the default TTL)), max-age (Cache-Control: max-age), no-store (Cache-Control: no-store).

originMaxAge.title: Origin max-age
originMaxAge.description: The max-age the origin sends when it sends one. An assumption: it depends on your application. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

errorMinTtl.title: Error caching minimum TTL
errorMinTtl.description: How long CloudFront caches a 404, 414, 500, 501, 502, 503 or 504 from the origin before asking again. AWS's default is 10 s; the upper bound here is an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

staleWhileRevalidate.title: stale-while-revalidate
staleWhileRevalidate.description: When the origin sends stale-while-revalidate, an expired object is served for this long while one request refreshes it. 0 for none. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

staleIfError.title: stale-if-error
staleIfError.description: When the origin sends stale-if-error, an expired object is served for this long past its expiry if the origin is failing. 0 for none (CloudFront still serves a stale object for the error caching TTL when the origin returns a 5xx). A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

locations.title: Edge locations hit
locations.description: How many edge locations (POPs) the viewers spread over. Each has its own cache, so more locations means more cold caches and a lower hit ratio at the edge. The more viewers are spread around the world, the more of these.

capacity.title: Edge cache capacity
capacity.description: Objects one edge location keeps before it evicts the least recently requested. AWS does not publish cache sizes, so this is an assumption. In objects.

latency.title: Edge processing time
latency.description: What the edge location itself adds to every request (TLS, cache lookup, headers). The viewer's network distance is the latency of the edge from the client. AWS publishes no figure, so this is an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

priceClass.title: Price class
priceClass.description: Which edge locations may serve the distribution. Viewers near regions a class leaves out are served from a farther edge location and are slower. How many viewers that is, is an assumption (0%, 10%, 25%). One of: all (Price Class All), 200 (Price Class 200), 100 (Price Class 100).

farLatency.title: Extra latency from a farther edge
farLatency.description: What a viewer outside the price class's regions pays on top of the normal latency. An assumption: about one more intercontinental round trip.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

enabled.title: Regional edge cache
enabled.description: The larger middle tier between edge locations and the origin. CloudFront uses it automatically for cacheable GET and HEAD requests; proxied methods skip it.

locations.title: Regional edge caches hit
locations.description: How many regional caches the edge locations are spread over. Edge location i uses cache i mod this. AWS does not publish the mapping, so it is a modelling choice.

capacity.title: Regional cache capacity
capacity.description: AWS says it is larger than an edge location's cache and publishes no figure: an assumption. In objects.

hop.title: Edge to regional cache latency
hop.description: One way. An assumption: both are close to the viewers.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

capacity.title: Origin Shield capacity
capacity.description: Objects each Origin Shield keeps. AWS does not publish it: an assumption. Turn Origin Shield on per origin, on its edge. In objects.

hop.title: Regional cache to Origin Shield latency
hop.description: One way. The shield sits in the region with the lowest latency to the origin, so it is typically farther from the viewers. An assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

enabled.title: Compress objects automatically
enabled.description: Gzip or Brotli for objects between 1,000 and 10,000,000 bytes of a compressible type, so fewer bytes reach the viewer. Viewers must send Accept-Encoding; the model assumes they do.

ratio.title: Compressed size
ratio.description: What a compressible object shrinks to, as a share of its size. AWS says 'less than a quarter' in some cases; the default is an assumption for text. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

compressibleShare.title: Compressible share
compressibleShare.description: The share of the response bytes that are of a type CloudFront compresses (HTML, JS, CSS, JSON... but not JPEG or video). An assumption; the model uses the expected value. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

clientErrors.title: On 4xx (400, 403, 404, 416, 429)
clientErrors.description: Origin group failover criteria. Used when an origin is set to be the secondary.

status503.title: On 503 (and when CloudFront cannot connect)
status503.description: AWS fails over on a failed connection only when 503 is selected.

status504.title: On 504 (and origin timeouts)
status504.description: AWS fails over on an origin timeout only when 504 is selected.

viewerRequest.title: Viewer request
viewerRequest.description: Code that runs on every request before the cache lookup. One of: none (None), function (CloudFront Function), lambda (Lambda@Edge).

viewerResponse.title: Viewer response
viewerResponse.description: Code that runs on every response before it goes to the viewer. One of: none (None), function (CloudFront Function), lambda (Lambda@Edge).

originRequest.title: Origin request
originRequest.description: Lambda@Edge that runs only on a cache miss, before the request goes to the origin. One of: none (None), lambda (Lambda@Edge).

originResponse.title: Origin response
originResponse.description: Lambda@Edge that runs only on a cache miss, when the origin has answered. One of: none (None), lambda (Lambda@Edge).

cloudFrontFunction.title: CloudFront Function time
cloudFrontFunction.description: AWS says CloudFront Functions run in under a millisecond; the distribution is an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

lambdaAtEdge.title: Lambda@Edge time
lambdaAtEdge.description: Includes the occasional cold start. AWS publishes no figure for how long Lambda@Edge takes, so this is an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

lambdaTimeout.title: Lambda@Edge timeout
lambdaTimeout.description: A function that runs longer fails and the viewer gets a 503. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

errorRate.title: Function error rate
errorRate.description: Share of executions that fail. The viewer gets a 503, which AWS documents for execution errors. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

every.title: Invalidate every
every.description: Purge the cache on a schedule, as a deploy pipeline might. 0 for never. A wildcard path counts as one invalidation path however many objects it covers. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

share.title: Share of objects invalidated
share.description: 1 is '/*'. Less is a set of specific paths covering that share of the objects. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

propagation.title: Propagation time
propagation.description: How long an invalidation takes to reach every edge location and regional cache. AWS publishes no figure (it says invalidations propagate to every location), so this is an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

purgeVersion.title: Purge now
purgeVersion.description: Change this number while running to invalidate everything now. It is the button for 'create invalidation /*'.

aws.route53.settings.description: Settings of Route 53 record: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

policy.title: Policy
policy.description: How Route 53 picks the record it answers with. Each edge on the out port is one record. Simple routing returns the values in random order and does not health-check them. One of: simple (Simple (values in random order, no health checks)), weighted (Weighted (by each record's weight)), failover (Failover (primary, then secondary)), latency (Latency (the endpoint nearest the callers)), geolocation (Geolocation (by the callers' continent)).

ttl.title: TTL
ttl.description: How long resolvers cache an answer before asking Route 53 again. AWS recommends 60 seconds or less for records with a health check; 60 s is also the TTL of an alias to a load balancer. 0 means every call asks. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

type.title: Type
type.description: HTTP: a connection within 4 s, then a 2xx or 3xx within 2 s of connecting. TCP: only a connection, within 10 s, so an endpoint that answers every request with a 500 still passes. One of: http (HTTP or HTTPS), tcp (TCP).

interval.title: Interval
interval.description: Seconds between one health checker's response and its next request. Only 10 or 30 (hard); AWS's default is 30. One of: 30 (Standard (30 seconds)), 10 (Fast (10 seconds, costs more)).

failureThreshold.title: Failure threshold
failureThreshold.description: Consecutive checks a health checker must see fail (or pass) before it changes its mind. AWS's default is 3. A hard limit of the provider.

regions.title: Health checker regions
regions.description: How many regions check each endpoint. With none chosen AWS uses all eight; you must keep at least three. In regions. A hard limit of the provider.

checkersPerRegion.title: Checkers per region
checkersPerRegion.description: AWS does not publish how many health checkers each region runs. It says that at a 30 second interval an endpoint gets a check about every two seconds, which is about 15 checkers, so 2 in each of 8 regions. An assumption.

count.title: Resolver caches
count.description: How many DNS caches (recursive resolvers, and the caches in clients' own stub resolvers) the callers are spread over. Each caches its own answer, and they expire at different times, so a change reaches the traffic gradually over one TTL. A weighted split is a split of these caches. An assumption.

lookup.title: Lookup time on a cache miss
lookup.description: What a call waits when its resolver has no live answer and asks Route 53. Calls answered from a cache wait nothing: Route 53 is not in the data path. An assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

ignoreTtlShare.title: Resolvers that ignore the TTL
ignoreTtlShare.description: The share of caches that keep an answer longer than its TTL (some ISP resolvers, a JVM caching for the life of the process). They go on sending traffic to an endpoint after everyone else has moved. How many there are is an assumption. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

ignoreTtlFor.title: They keep answers for
ignoreTtlFor.description: How long a resolver that ignores the TTL keeps an answer. An assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

aws.waf.settings.description: Settings of WAF web ACL: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

protects.title: Protects
protects.description: What the web ACL is associated with: put the WAF in front of it. A CloudFront web ACL is global (created in us-east-1), so leave it outside region boxes like CloudFront; the others are regional and belong in the protected resource's region. It decides the body inspection limit (8 KB fixed for ALB and AppSync) and whether the regional request quota applies. One of: cloudfront (CloudFront distribution (global)), alb (Application Load Balancer), apigateway (API Gateway REST API), appsync (AppSync GraphQL API), cognito (Cognito user pool), apprunner (App Runner service), verifiedaccess (Verified Access instance).

latency.title: Inspection latency
latency.description: What evaluating the web ACL adds to each request. AWS publishes no figure: an assumption. The association is modelled as a hop, so the edge into the protected resource adds its own (1 ms inside a region; set it to 0 for none).

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

requestRate.title: Requests per second (web ACL)
requestRate.description: Regional web ACLs only. Past it AWS WAF cannot take the request, which the protected resource answers as an ALB does when the web ACL fails: 500, or the request goes through uninspected with fail-open (what happens past the quota is not documented: an assumption). For CloudFront the developer guide says CloudFront sets the limit, so it is not applied here. In req/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

failOpen.title: Fail open (ALB)
failOpen.description: The load balancer attribute waf.fail_open.enabled: when the ALB cannot hand a request to AWS WAF it routes it to its targets uninspected instead of answering 500. Application Load Balancers only (default off).

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: One rate-based rule, aggregating on the client IP address, evaluated before every other rule.

limit.title: Rate limit
limit.description: Requests one address may make in the evaluation window. Over it, the address is rate limited until its count falls back under. AWS has no default: 2,000 is an example. In requests. A hard limit of the provider.

window.title: Evaluation window
window.description: How far back AWS WAF counts each time it checks. It checks about every 10 seconds whatever the window. One of: 60 (1 minute), 120 (2 minutes), 300 (5 minutes (AWS default)), 600 (10 minutes).

scope.title: Scope-down
scope.description: Count and rate limit only these requests, with a scope-down statement on the HTTP method (2 WCUs). A request's method is its operation. One of: all (Every request), write (Writes only (POST, PUT...: a login or signup)), read (Reads only (GET)).

action.title: Action
action.description: What happens to a rate-limited address's requests. Count only counts them, the way a new rule is tested. One of: block (Block (403)), count (Count (watch, don't block)).

lag.title: Propagation delay
lag.description: How long after a check AWS WAF starts (or stops) rate limiting an address, on top of checking every 10 seconds. AWS says the delay is usually under 30 seconds and can be several minutes: an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

traffic.title: Traffic as AWS WAF sees it

addresses.title: Addresses per traffic source
addresses.description: A request carries no IP address, so each traffic source (the client that made it) is taken to send from this many addresses, a request's key choosing one. A client's hot key always lands on one address: one IP flooding. A source spread over many addresses stays under a per-IP limit. A modelling choice.

attackSources.title: Attack traffic from
attackSources.description: Ids of traffic sources (client nodes) whose requests are attacks: scanners, injection attempts, bad bots. The rules match them at the attack match share below. Comma separated.

core.title: Core
core.description: OWASP-style protections for any web application. Its SizeRestrictions_BODY rule blocks bodies over 8 KB. 700 WCUs.

coreBodySize.title: Core: SizeRestrictions_BODY
coreBodySize.description: The Core rule set blocks any request body over 8,192 bytes, uploads included. Overriding this one rule to Count is the usual fix. One of: block (Block (the group's action)), count (Override to Count).

knownBadInputs.title: Known bad inputs
knownBadInputs.description: Request patterns known to be invalid or exploits (Log4j, Java deserialization). 200 WCUs.

adminProtection.title: Admin protection
adminProtection.description: Blocks access to exposed admin pages. 100 WCUs.

windows.title: Windows
windows.description: Windows and PowerShell command injection. 200 WCUs.

ipReputation.title: Ip reputation
ipReputation.description: Addresses Amazon's threat intelligence knows as malicious. 25 WCUs.

anonymousIp.title: Anonymous ip
anonymousIp.description: VPNs, proxies, Tor and hosting providers. 50 WCUs.

botControl.title: Bot control
botControl.description: Self-identifying bots (common level); charged extra. Only its matching is modelled. 50 WCUs.

customWcu.title: Your own rules
customWcu.description: Capacity your own rules and rule groups use (IP sets, string and regex matches, geo matches...). They match like the managed groups below. In WCU.

action.title: Action
action.description: What the managed rule groups and your rules do with a request they match. Count only counts, the way new rules are tried out. One of: block (Block (403)), count (Count (override every rule to Count)).

match.title: Match share (other traffic)
match.description: Share of ordinary requests that some rule matches: bad requests mixed into the traffic, or false positives. An assumption about your traffic, like an SNS filter's match share. Nothing matches when there are no rules. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

attackMatch.title: Match share (attack traffic)
attackMatch.description: Share of requests from the attack sources that the rules catch, when every byte of them is inspected. An assumption. Nothing matches when there are no rules. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

inspectionLimit.title: Body inspection limit
inspectionLimit.description: How much of a request body AWS WAF inspects, for CloudFront, API Gateway, Cognito, App Runner and Verified Access. Fixed at 8 KB for ALB and AppSync (this is then ignored). Raising it costs extra for bodies over 16 KB. The rules miss an attack hidden past the limit. One of: 16 (16 KB (default)), 32 (32 KB), 48 (48 KB), 64 (64 KB).

blockOversize.title: Block oversized bodies
blockOversize.description: A size constraint rule (1 WCU) placed before the rule groups that blocks any body over the inspection limit, as AWS recommends, so nothing uninspected gets through. Legitimate large uploads are blocked too.

aws.alb.settings.description: Settings of Application Load Balancer: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

zones.title: Availability Zones
zones.description: Zones the load balancer has a node in: the first ones of its region (a, b, c...). Clients spread over the nodes through DNS. A zone outage takes its node away; with cross-zone off a node only sends to targets in its own zone. An ALB needs at least two. In zones. A hard limit of the provider.

routing.title: Routing
routing.description: How a request picks its target group (an edge). Weighted: at random by the edges' weights, as a forward action to several target groups does (blue/green, canary). Rules: by the request's key, an edge's weight being the share of requests its rule matches, so one path (key) always reaches the same target group. One of: weighted (Weighted target groups (one forward action)), rules (Listener rules (path or host conditions)).

rules.title: Listener rules
rules.description: Rules the listener evaluates for each request (besides the default rule). Only their cost is modelled: past 10, rule evaluations count towards LCUs. In rules. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

idleTimeout.title: Idle timeout
idleTimeout.description: How long the load balancer waits for its target to start answering before it gives up with 504 (the target keeps working). Lambda targets are waited for until they answer. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

overhead.title: Load balancer processing time
overhead.description: Time the load balancer itself adds to a request (request and response processing time in its access logs). AWS publishes no figure: an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

requestsPerConnection.title: Requests per connection
requestsPerConnection.description: How many requests a client sends over one connection before opening another (keep-alive). It turns the request rate into new connections a second, one of the dimensions LCUs are counted in. An assumption: clients that reuse connections send many; 1 is a new connection per request. In requests.

model.title: Model scaling
model.description: Give the load balancer a capacity that follows its traffic with a lag, so a sudden surge finds it short and some connections are rejected while it scales. AWS publishes how capacity is counted (LCUs) but not how fast it scales: the numbers below are assumptions. Off: unlimited capacity.

reserved.title: LCU reservation
reserved.description: Capacity reserved ahead of an event: the load balancer never has less. 0 is none; a reservation is at least 100 LCUs. Needs the Region's reserved-LCU quota raised (it is 0 by default). In LCU. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

minimum.title: Minimum capacity
minimum.description: The capacity the load balancer keeps however quiet it is, and starts with if it has no traffic. An assumption: AWS doesn't publish it. (It starts scaled to the traffic of its first second.) In LCU.

scaleUpPerMinute.title: Scale-up rate
scaleUpPerMinute.description: How much capacity can grow in a minute while demand is above it: 2 is doubling every minute. An assumption: AWS doesn't publish how fast an ALB scales. In × a minute.

aws.nlb.settings.description: Settings of Network Load Balancer: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

zones.title: Availability Zones
zones.description: Zones the load balancer has a node in: the first ones of its region. Clients spread over them through DNS; with cross-zone off (the NLB default) each node only sends to targets in its own zone. In zones.

idleTimeout.title: TCP idle timeout
idleTimeout.description: A connection with nothing sent either way for this long is forgotten, and the next packet on it gets a reset. Here: a request whose target hasn't answered in this long is reset. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

overhead.title: Load balancer processing time
overhead.description: Time the load balancer adds to a connection. AWS calls it ultra-low and publishes no figure: 0 by default (an assumption), the network on the edges being the cost.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

It turns the request rate into new connections a second, one of the dimensions LCUs are counted in. An assumption: clients that reuse connections send many; 1 is a new connection per request. In requests.
