minSize.title: Minimum size
minSize.description: MinSize: the group never has fewer, whatever its desired capacity says. In instances.

maxSize.title: Maximum size
maxSize.description: MaxSize: the group never has more, except briefly while rebalancing zones (up to 10% or one instance over). A warm pool holds MaxSize minus desired by default. In instances.

desiredCapacity.title: Desired capacity
desiredCapacity.description: How many instances it should run, kept between the minimum and maximum. A target-tracking controller drives this (setting: desiredCapacity). Instances it adds take the launch time to serve; instances it removes are terminated by the termination policy. In instances.

availabilityZones.title: Availability Zones
availabilityZones.description: The group's subnets: the first N zones of its region. Launches go to the zone with the fewest instances; a zone outage loses its instances, which are replaced in the other zones, and the group rebalances (AZRebalance) when the zone is back. In zones. A hard limit of the provider.

requestsPerVcpu.title: Requests per vCPU
requestsPerVcpu.description: How many requests one vCPU works on at once. 1 for CPU-bound work, where a request holds a vCPU for its service time and busy workers are CPU utilization; more for an application whose threads block on I/O. A modelling choice, not an AWS figure. In requests.

serviceTime.title: Service time
serviceTime.description: How long a request keeps a worker (a vCPU) busy, before any downstream calls. An instance releases the worker while it waits on downstream calls.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

queueLimit.title: Queue per instance
queueLimit.description: Requests that may wait for a worker on each instance (the server's accept backlog). Past it a request is refused with 503. Called through a plain edge, the group has one line of this many per serving instance. An assumption about the application. In requests.

errorRate.title: Error rate
errorRate.description: Fraction of requests the application fails (500) after working on them. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

fanOut.title: Downstream calls
fanOut.description: After its own work, call every output one after another, all at once, pick one by weight, or call none. One of: sequential (Sequential), parallel (Parallel), weighted (Weighted), none (None).

launch.title: Launch timings
launch.description: What a new instance goes through before it is InService: about three minutes by default. AWS publishes none of these numbers.

pending.title: Pending
pending.description: From the launch request until the instance is running: EC2 finds a host and starts it. AWS publishes no figure: an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

boot.title: Boot
boot.description: The operating system boots and cloud-init starts. An assumption: it depends on the AMI. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

userData.title: User data
userData.description: The user data script: installing packages, fetching the application and its configuration. The part a warm pool saves. An assumption: it is your script. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

appStart.title: Application start
appStart.description: The application starts and is ready to serve (and to pass a load balancer's health check). An assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

healthCheckType.title: Health check type
healthCheckType.description: EC2 (the default): an instance is replaced only when it stops running or fails its status checks. ELB: also when the load balancer's target group reports it unhealthy, so an instance whose application is broken is replaced too (wire it through a target group). One of: EC2 (EC2 status checks), ELB (EC2 and ELB health checks).

healthCheckGracePeriod.title: Health check grace period
healthCheckGracePeriod.description: How long after a new instance is InService before its health checks count. 300 seconds is the console's default; a group created with the CLI or an SDK gets 0. An instance found dead during it is replaced when it ends. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

statusCheckReplace.title: Replaces an impaired instance after
statusCheckReplace.description: How long until Auto Scaling replaces an instance that stopped answering (its zone failed, its host died). EC2 runs status checks every minute and Auto Scaling waits 'a few minutes' before acting: three is an assumption. With ELB health checks a target group may notice sooner. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

defaultInstanceWarmup.title: Instance warmup
defaultInstanceWarmup.description: How long after an instance is InService before its CPU counts in the group's average (the cpu gauge, and cpuTotal through it), so start-up doesn't skew scaling. Not set by default, in which case scaling policies use the default cooldown, 300 seconds: the default here. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

shutdownGrace.title: Shutdown grace
shutdownGrace.description: How long an instance being terminated (scale-in, replacement, rebalancing) has to finish its in-flight requests, when nothing else holds it (a target group holds it for its deregistration delay). The application's own SIGTERM handling: an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

terminationPolicy.title: Termination policy
terminationPolicy.description: Which instance goes on scale-in, after the zones are balanced (always first). Default: the purchase option out of proportion first, then the instance closest to its next billing hour. Oldest or newest instance. ClosestToNextInstanceHour. One of: Default (Default), OldestInstance (Oldest instance), NewestInstance (Newest instance), ClosestToNextInstanceHour (Closest to next instance hour).

brokenLaunches.title: Broken launches
brokenLaunches.description: Share of new instances whose application never becomes healthy: a bad AMI or launch template version, user data that fails. They run (EC2 status checks pass) but fail a load balancer's health checks and answer every request with 500. With ELB health checks they are replaced, again and again. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

warmPool.title: Warm pool
warmPool.description: Pre-initialised instances that start much faster than a launch. Not available with Spot Instances.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Keep pre-initialised instances beside the group, so a scale-out starts them instead of launching from scratch.

poolState.title: Pool state
poolState.description: Stopped: start, boot and start the application (user data already ran). Hibernated: start with memory restored, so the application is already up. Running: ready at once, but paid for and counted against the vCPU quota like any running instance. One of: Stopped (Stopped), Running (Running), Hibernated (Hibernated).

minSize.title: Minimum size
minSize.description: Instances kept in the pool however large the group is. AWS's default is none. In instances.

maxGroupPreparedCapacity.title: Maximum prepared capacity
maxGroupPreparedCapacity.description: The pool holds this minus the desired capacity (at least its minimum). 0: not set, so the pool holds the maximum size minus the desired capacity, AWS's default. In instances.

spot.title: Spot and On-Demand
spot.description: The group's instances distribution: how many are Spot, how often Spot is reclaimed (with a two-minute notice), and Capacity Rebalancing.

onDemandBaseCapacity.title: On-Demand base
onDemandBaseCapacity.description: The first instances of the group are On-Demand. AWS's default is 0. In instances.

onDemandPercentageAboveBase.title: On-Demand above base
onDemandPercentageAboveBase.description: The share of instances beyond the base that are On-Demand; the rest are Spot. A fraction rounds up in favour of On-Demand. AWS's default is 100: no Spot. In %. A hard limit of the provider.

interruptionsPerHour.title: Interruption rate
interruptionsPerHour.description: How often EC2 reclaims a Spot Instance. AWS's Spot Instance Advisor puts the historical average under 5% of instances a month, about 0.00007 an hour: the default, an assumption. Raise it for an interruption storm. In per instance-hour.

insufficientCapacity.title: Launches without capacity
insufficientCapacity.description: Share of Spot launch attempts EC2 can't fulfil (InsufficientInstanceCapacity). The group keeps retrying Spot; it never falls back to On-Demand. An assumption to set, not an AWS figure. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

capacityRebalance.title: Capacity Rebalancing
capacityRebalance.description: On a rebalance recommendation, launch a replacement and terminate the at-risk instance once the new one is InService, instead of waiting for the interruption. Off by default.

rebalanceLead.title: Recommendation lead
rebalanceLead.description: How long before the two-minute interruption notice the rebalance recommendation arrives. AWS says it may come earlier or with the notice, and publishes no figure: an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

scaleInProtection.title: Protect new instances from scale-in
scaleInProtection.description: NewInstancesProtectedFromScaleIn: instances the group launches while this is on are protected, so lowering the desired capacity terminates none of them and the group stays larger. Turning it off doesn't unprotect them (AWS's per-instance SetInstanceProtection isn't simulated). Health-check replacement and Spot interruptions still take them. Instances there at the start are not protected.

aws.ecs.settings.description: Settings of ECS service: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

desiredCount.title: Desired count
desiredCount.description: How many tasks the service keeps running. Service auto scaling (a target-tracking controller, setting: desiredCount) drives it. At most 5,000 tasks per service. In tasks. A hard limit of the provider.

launchType.title: Capacity
launchType.description: Fargate: each task gets its own capacity, counted against the region's Fargate vCPU quotas. EC2: tasks are placed on the container instances of an Auto Scaling group the service scales with managed scaling (the EC2 group below). Read when the simulation starts: a change applies on the next run. One of: FARGATE (Fargate), EC2 (EC2 (Auto Scaling group capacity provider)).

zones.title: Availability Zones
zones.description: The service's subnets are in this many zones of its region (the first ones). Tasks spread over them, the emptiest first, as ECS's default spread over ecs.availability-zone does; on EC2 the instances spread over them too. A zone outage takes the tasks there with it. In zones.

revision.title: Task definition revision
revision.description: Change it to deploy a new task definition: a rolling deployment replaces every task, within the deployment's minimum healthy and maximum percent. The image, start-up and failure below belong to the revision that is current when they are set.

cpu.title: CPU
cpu.description: The task's CPU (1,024 units to a vCPU). It sets how many requests a task works on at once (with requests per vCPU) and what it counts against the Fargate vCPU quota, or takes on an instance. One of: 256 (0.25 vCPU), 512 (0.5 vCPU), 1024 (1 vCPU), 2048 (2 vCPU), 4096 (4 vCPU), 8192 (8 vCPU), 16384 (16 vCPU), 32768 (32 vCPU).

memory.title: Memory
memory.description: The task's memory. Fargate accepts only certain pairs: 0.25 vCPU with 512, 1024 or 2048 MiB; 0.5 vCPU 1-4 GB; 1 vCPU 2-8 GB; 2 vCPU 4-16 GB; 4 vCPU 8-30 GB (1 GB steps); 8 vCPU 16-60 GB (4 GB steps); 16 vCPU 32-120 GB (8 GB steps); 32 vCPU 60, 120 or 244 GB. Other values run as the next size up (the design check says so). On EC2 it is what an instance must have free. In MiB. A hard limit of the provider.

requestsPerVcpu.title: Requests per vCPU
requestsPerVcpu.description: How many requests a task works on at once, per vCPU (at least one per task): its threads or event loop's practical limit. CPU utilization is the share of them busy. An assumption about your application. In requests.

serviceTime.title: Service time
serviceTime.description: How long a request keeps one of the task's workers busy, before any downstream calls.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

imageSize.title: Image size
imageSize.description: The container image, compressed. Fargate keeps no image cache, so every task pulls all of it; pull time grows with size (AWS recommends lazy loading over 250 MiB). On EC2 a task on an instance that already has the image skips the download. In MiB.

lazyLoading.title: SOCI lazy loading
lazyLoading.description: Seekable OCI: the task starts after pulling only an index and fetches the rest as it is read, so containers 'only spend a few seconds on the image pull'. Needs Fargate platform 1.4.0 and a private ECR image with a SOCI index.

pullRate.title: Pull rate
pullRate.description: How fast an image is downloaded and unpacked. An assumption: AWS publishes none (a large image on EC2 'might take 10-20 seconds'). In MiB/s.

appStart.title: Application start
appStart.description: From the container starting until the application serves. An assumption about your application. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

failure.title: What's wrong with it
failure.description: A bad revision. Crashes: the essential container exits as it starts, so the task stops before RUNNING. Fails its health checks: it runs, answers every request with 500, and its container health check marks it UNHEALTHY after 90 s (3 checks 30 s apart; a target group's checks may find it sooner). ECS replaces such tasks; the deployment circuit breaker counts them. One of: none (None: it works), crash (Crashes as it starts), unhealthy (Fails its health checks).

queueLimit.title: Queue limit
queueLimit.description: Requests that may wait for a free worker: in one line in front of the service when it is called directly, or in front of each task when a load balancer's target group picks tasks. Beyond it they are refused at once with 503. An assumption about your application's accept queue. In requests.

fanOut.title: Downstream calls
fanOut.description: After its own work, call every output one after another, all at once, pick one by weight, or call none. One of: sequential (Sequential), parallel (Parallel), weighted (Weighted), none (None).

healthCheckGracePeriod.title: Health check grace period
healthCheckGracePeriod.description: healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds: how long after a task starts ECS ignores failing load balancer and container health checks. Default 0 (AWS allows up to 2,147,483,647 s). A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

stopTimeout.title: Stop timeout
stopTimeout.description: From SIGTERM to SIGKILL when a task is stopped (scaled in, replaced, deployed over, or interrupted on Fargate Spot): it takes no new requests and finishes what it holds meanwhile. 30 s by default, 2-120 s on Fargate. A load balancer's deregistration delay can keep a draining task longer. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

lostTaskDetection.title: Notices a lost task after
lostTaskDetection.description: How long until ECS notices on its own that a task died with its host or zone and starts another. An assumption: AWS publishes no figure. A target group's health checks may notice sooner. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

minimumHealthyPercent.title: Minimum healthy percent
minimumHealthyPercent.description: During a deployment, at least this share of the desired count (rounded up) stays healthy: old tasks are stopped only while it holds. A new task counts as healthy 40 s after it is RUNNING. In %. A hard limit of the provider.

maximumPercent.title: Maximum percent
maximumPercent.description: During a deployment, at most this share of the desired count (rounded down) runs or is pending, old and new together: room to start new tasks before stopping old ones. AWS publishes no upper bound; the simulator allows 1,000%. In %. A hard limit of the provider.

circuitBreaker.title: Deployment circuit breaker
circuitBreaker.description: Fail a deployment whose new tasks keep failing: half the desired count of failures (at least 3, at most 200), counting tasks that stop before RUNNING and tasks that fail health checks. A healthy new task resets the count. A failed deployment launches no more new tasks.

rollback.title: Roll back on failure
rollback.description: With the circuit breaker: a failed deployment rolls back to the last revision that completed, replacing the failed revision's tasks.

base.title: FARGATE base
base.description: The first tasks always run on Fargate (On-Demand) capacity; the rest are split by weight. In tasks. A hard limit of the provider.

weight.title: FARGATE weight
weight.description: Relative share of tasks beyond the base on Fargate (On-Demand). 0 places none there. A hard limit of the provider.

spotWeight.title: FARGATE_SPOT weight
spotWeight.description: Relative share of tasks beyond the base on Fargate Spot: spare capacity at a discount, taken back with a two-minute warning. Fargate never falls back to On-Demand when Spot is short; the tasks wait. A hard limit of the provider.

spotInterruptionsPerTaskHour.title: Spot interruptions
spotInterruptionsPerTaskHour.description: How often a Fargate Spot task is interrupted. AWS publishes no rate: the default is EC2's Spot Instance Advisor's under 5% a month, an assumption. Raise it in a scenario for an interruption wave. Each interrupted task gets SIGTERM at the warning and stops after its stop timeout; a replacement starts at once, on whatever capacity the strategy picks. In per task-hour.

maxSize.title: Maximum size
maxSize.description: At most 5,000 container instances per cluster. In instances. A hard limit of the provider.

desiredSize.title: Instances at the start
desiredSize.description: How many instances the group runs when the simulation starts. Managed scaling moves it from there. In instances.

managedScaling.title: Managed scaling
managedScaling.description: ECS scales the group on CapacityProviderReservation (instances needed ÷ instances running × 100) toward the target capacity: out after one minute's data point, in after 15 minutes of them and 15 minutes after a scale-out. Off: the group stays at its starting size.

targetCapacity.title: Target capacity
targetCapacity.description: 100: no spare instances. Lower keeps spare ones, so new tasks start without waiting for an instance (90: about a tenth spare). In %. A hard limit of the provider.

minimumScalingStepSize.title: Minimum scaling step
minimumScalingStepSize.description: In instances. A hard limit of the provider.

maximumScalingStepSize.title: Maximum scaling step
maximumScalingStepSize.description: In instances. A hard limit of the provider.

managedTerminationProtection.title: Managed termination protection
managedTerminationProtection.description: Instances running tasks are protected from scale-in: only empty ones are terminated, so the group may stay larger than managed scaling asks until binpacking empties some.

managedDraining.title: Managed instance draining
managedDraining.description: An instance being terminated is drained first: its tasks are replaced elsewhere and stop gracefully. On by default. Off: they stop with the instance.

placement.title: Placement strategy
placement.description: Within a zone, the instance with the most room (spread on instanceId) or the least memory left that fits (binpack), which empties whole instances for scale-in. Zones come first either way, as ECS's default spread over ecs.availability-zone does (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-placement-strategies.html). One of: spread (Spread over instances), binpack (Binpack on memory).

pending.title: Instance pending
pending.description: From launch until EC2 reports it running. An assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

boot.title: Instance boot
boot.description: The operating system boots. An assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

register.title: Agent registers
register.description: The ECS container agent starts and registers the instance with the cluster: then tasks can be placed on it. An assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

replaceAfter.title: Replaces a failed instance after
replaceAfter.description: How long until the group finds an instance dead (EC2 status checks) and replaces it; its tasks are replaced then too, if ECS hasn't already. An assumption: AWS says it waits "a few minutes" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/health-checks-overview.html). A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

aws.eks.settings.description: Settings of EKS workload: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

replicas.title: Replicas
replicas.description: The Deployment's replicas. The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (a target-tracking controller, setting: replicas) drives it. In pods.

zones.title: Availability Zones
zones.description: The node group's subnets are in this many zones of its region (the first ones); nodes spread over them, and pods over the nodes. In zones.

revision.title: Pod template revision
revision.description: Change it to roll out a new pod template: a rolling update replaces every pod, at most maxSurge over and maxUnavailable under the replicas. The image, start-up and failure below belong to the revision current when they are set.

cpu.title: CPU request
cpu.description: What the scheduler reserves on a node for each pod, and what CPU utilization is relative to (the HPA's target is a share of the request). It also sets how many requests a pod works on at once. In millicores.

memory.title: Memory request
memory.description: What the scheduler reserves on a node for each pod. In MiB.

requestsPerCore.title: Requests per core
requestsPerCore.description: How many requests a pod works on at once per core of its CPU request (at least one per pod). An assumption about your application. Pods don't burst past their request here. In requests.

serviceTime.title: Service time
serviceTime.description: How long a request keeps one of the pod's workers busy, before any downstream calls.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

imageSize.title: Image size
imageSize.description: The container image, compressed. A node pulls it once (imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent): the first pod on a new node waits for the whole download, later ones start at once. In MiB.

pullRate.title: Pull rate
pullRate.description: How fast a node downloads and unpacks an image. An assumption. In MiB/s.

appStart.title: Application start
appStart.description: From the container starting until the application would pass its readiness probe. An assumption about your application. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

failure.title: What's wrong with it
failure.description: A bad revision. Crashes: the container exits as it starts and the kubelet restarts it with a back-off (10 s, 20 s, 40 s... up to 5 minutes), so the pod never becomes ready. Never ready: it runs but fails its readiness probe. Either way it takes no traffic, and a rolling update stalls with maxUnavailable old pods gone; Kubernetes doesn't roll back. One of: none (None: it works), crash (Crashes (CrashLoopBackOff)), unready (Never ready).

initialDelay.title: Initial delay
initialDelay.description: initialDelaySeconds: no probe before it. Default 0. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

period.title: Period
period.description: periodSeconds: a pod is ready at the first probe after its application is up. Default 10 s. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

queueLimit.title: Queue limit
queueLimit.description: Requests that may wait for a free worker: in one line in front of the Service when it is called directly, or per pod when a load balancer's target group picks pods. Beyond it, 503. An assumption about your application. In requests.

fanOut.title: Downstream calls
fanOut.description: After its own work, call every output one after another, all at once, pick one by weight, or call none. One of: sequential (Sequential), parallel (Parallel), weighted (Weighted), none (None).

terminationGracePeriod.title: Termination grace period
terminationGracePeriod.description: terminationGracePeriodSeconds: a pod being stopped (scaled in, evicted, rolled over) takes no new requests and has this long to finish what it holds. Default 30 s. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

maxSurge.title: Max surge
maxSurge.description: Pods over replicas during a rollout, as a share rounded up. Default 25%. In %. A hard limit of the provider.

maxUnavailable.title: Max unavailable
maxUnavailable.description: Pods under replicas that may be unavailable during a rollout, as a share rounded down. Default 25%. It can't be 0 when max surge is. In %. A hard limit of the provider.

topologySpread.title: Topology spread
topologySpread.description: How pods spread over zones. Best effort: the zone with the fewest first, others if it has no room (the scheduler's default constraint, ScheduleAnyway). Strict: a topology spread constraint with maxSkew 1 and whenUnsatisfiable DoNotSchedule: a pod waits as Pending rather than skew the zones (https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/topology-spread-constraints/). One of: zones (Across zones, best effort), strict (Across zones, maxSkew 1 (DoNotSchedule)), none (None).

monitorGracePeriod.title: Node monitor grace period
monitorGracePeriod.description: --node-monitor-grace-period: a node that stops reporting is NotReady after this long. 50 s since Kubernetes 1.32 (40 s before). A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

tolerationSeconds.title: Toleration of a NotReady node
tolerationSeconds.description: tolerationSeconds for the not-ready and unreachable taints, 300 s by default: how long a pod stays bound to a failed node before it is evicted and the ReplicaSet replaces it. Pods on a dead node are replaced this long after it is NotReady (5 min 50 s in all), or sooner if the node is replaced. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

maxSize.title: Maximum size
maxSize.description: What the autoscaler may grow to: the node group's maximum size, or Karpenter's NodePool limit. 450 nodes per managed node group by default (adjustable). In nodes. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

desiredSize.title: Nodes at the start
desiredSize.description: How many nodes run when the simulation starts. The autoscaler moves it from there. In nodes.

maxPods.title: Max pods per node
maxPods.description: The VPC CNI gives each pod an address, so a node holds ENIs × (IPs per ENI − 1) + 2 pods: 29 for a large instance (m5.large, m7i.large), more for bigger ones. Set it for your instance type. It also sets the memory the kubelet reserves (11 MiB a pod). In pods. A hard limit of the provider.

scheduling.title: Scheduler scoring
scheduling.description: Within a zone, the node with the most room (the scheduler's default, LeastAllocated) or the least (MostAllocated), which empties nodes for scale-down (https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/resource-bin-packing/). One of: spread (Least allocated (spread)), binpack (Most allocated (bin packing)).

autoscaler.title: Node autoscaler
autoscaler.description: What adds nodes when pods are Pending and removes the ones not needed. Cluster Autoscaler: scans every 10 s and changes the node group's size; removes a node under 50% requested after 10 minutes. Karpenter: batches pending pods (1-10 s), launches nodes directly, and consolidates nodes whose pods fit elsewhere at once. One of: cluster-autoscaler (Cluster Autoscaler), karpenter (Karpenter), none (None).

pending.title: Instance pending
pending.description: A node group instance, from launch until EC2 reports it running. An assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

boot.title: Instance boot
boot.description: The operating system boots. An assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

join.title: Joins the cluster
join.description: nodeadm configures the kubelet, which registers the node; the CNI starts; the node is Ready and pods can be scheduled on it. An assumption (EKS says 'multiple minutes' for a node; it must bootstrap within 15). A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

karpenterLaunch.title: Karpenter node ready
karpenterLaunch.description: A node Karpenter launches, from its decision until Ready. An assumption: the EKS docs say Karpenter provisions nodes 'in under a minute'. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

replaceAfter.title: Replaces a failed node after
replaceAfter.description: How long until a dead instance is found (EC2 status checks) and replaced, which takes its pods off the cluster at once. An assumption ('a few minutes'). A zone that is cut off may leave its instances passing their own checks: set it longer to see Kubernetes' own eviction instead. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

scanInterval.title: Scan interval
scanInterval.description: A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

scaleDownUnneededTime.title: Scale-down unneeded time
scaleDownUnneededTime.description: A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

scaleDownDelayAfterAdd.title: Scale-down delay after add
scaleDownDelayAfterAdd.description: A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

scaleDownUtilizationThreshold.title: Scale-down utilization threshold
scaleDownUtilizationThreshold.description: A node whose pods request less than this share of its allocatable CPU and memory, and whose pods fit on other nodes, is unneeded. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

batchIdle.title: Batch idle duration
batchIdle.description: A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

batchMax.title: Batch max duration
batchMax.description: A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

consolidation.title: Consolidation policy
consolidation.description: WhenEmptyOrUnderutilized: remove any node whose pods fit on the others. WhenEmpty: only nodes with no pods. One of: WhenEmptyOrUnderutilized (When empty or underutilized), WhenEmpty (When empty).

consolidateAfter.title: Consolidate after
consolidateAfter.description: How long after its pods last changed a node may be consolidated. Default 0. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

budget.title: Disruption budget
budget.description: At most this share of nodes is being consolidated at once. Default 10% (at least one). In %. A hard limit of the provider.

aws.lambda.settings.description: Settings of Lambda function: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

memory.title: Memory
memory.description: CPU is proportional to memory: one full vCPU at 1,769 MB. In MB. A hard limit of the provider.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: The invocation is killed when it runs this long, and its execution environment is discarded. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

duration.title: Handler duration
duration.description: How long the handler takes at 1,769 MB or more, excluding cold starts.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

cpuBound.title: CPU-bound share
cpuBound.description: How much of the handler's time is CPU work, which slows down below 1,769 MB. The rest (waiting on I/O) doesn't. A modelling choice, not an AWS figure. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

init.title: Init duration
init.description: Creating an environment and running initialisation code. AWS says 'under 100 ms to over 1 s' and gives no model, so this is an assumption. An init that runs past the 10 s limit is retried inside the first invocation, under the function timeout.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

idleTtl.title: Idle lifetime
idleTtl.description: How long an unused environment stays warm. AWS doesn't publish this number; it says only 'some time'. An assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

maxLifetime.title: Maximum lifetime
maxLifetime.description: Lambda retires environments every few hours, even busy ones, so each one is eventually replaced by a cold start. AWS publishes no number, so 0 (the default) turns this off; try a few hours. An assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

snapStart.title: SnapStart
snapStart.description: Resume new environments from a snapshot taken when the version was published, instead of running Init. Has no effect with provisioned concurrency, which AWS doesn't support alongside it.

restore.title: Restore duration
restore.description: Resuming an environment from a snapshot (SnapStart). AWS says only 'as low as sub-second', so this is an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Hold back part of the regional concurrency for this function, which also caps it. 0 throttles it entirely.

concurrency.title: Reserved concurrency
concurrency.description: In executions. A hard limit of the provider.

provisioned.title: Provisioned concurrency
provisioned.description: Execution environments kept initialised, so these never cold start. Counts against the regional concurrency, and can't exceed the reservation (it is clamped to it). In executions. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

provisionedAllocation.title: Provisioned allocation delay
provisionedAllocation.description: When provisioned concurrency is raised while running, the new environments become ready after this long, plus the time to allocate them at 6,000 a minute. AWS says 'a minute or two of preparation', so 90 s is a midpoint assumption. A design starts with its provisioned concurrency already allocated. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

rpsLimit.title: Enforce requests-per-second limit
rpsLimit.description: AWS allows 10 synchronous requests per second for each unit of concurrency (so 10,000 rps at the default 1,000), and answers 429 beyond it. Off by default; turn it on to see short, hot functions hit the request-rate ceiling before the concurrency one.

errorRate.title: Baseline error rate
errorRate.description: Chance that an invocation ends in an unhandled error (or, per record, see Batches). A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

fanOut.title: Downstream calls
fanOut.description: After the handler runs: call every output one after another, all at once, pick one by weight, or call none. One of: sequential (Sequential), parallel (Parallel), weighted (Weighted), none (None).

batchCalls.title: Batch downstream calls
batchCalls.description: When invoked with a batch of records (from SQS), call downstream once per record, or once carrying the whole batch. One of: each (One per record), once (One per batch).

duration.title: Handler duration is
duration.description: With a batch of records, take the handler duration once, or once for every record in the batch. One of: invocation (Per invocation), record (Per record).

errors.title: Error rate is
errors.description: With a batch of records, roll the error rate once, or once per record. Per record, any failing record fails the whole batch. Reported: the handler catches each record's error (and each record's failed downstream call) and returns the failed records as batch item failures, so the invocation succeeds; only an event source mapping with 'Report batch item failures' on acts on them, otherwise they are deleted with the rest. One of: invocation (Per invocation), record (Per record), report (Reported).

maxRetries.title: Retries
maxRetries.description: How many times a failed asynchronous invocation is retried. A hard limit of the provider.

firstRetryDelay.title: Delay before first retry
firstRetryDelay.description: AWS waits one minute between the first and second attempt. Only retries after function errors (including timeouts) wait; throttled events back off from 1 s to 5 minutes instead. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

secondRetryDelay.title: Delay before second retry
secondRetryDelay.description: AWS waits two minutes between the second and third attempt. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

maxEventAge.title: Max event age
maxEventAge.description: Events not processed within this (because of throttling, or retries) are discarded to the failure destination. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

aws.sqs.settings.description: Settings of SQS queue: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: FIFO delivers one message per message group at a time, and is rate-limited. The type is fixed when the queue is created (a standard queue can't be turned into a FIFO one). One of: standard (Standard), fifo (FIFO).

retention.title: Message retention
retention.description: Messages are deleted this long after they were enqueued, whether or not they were received. A standard dead-letter queue counts from the message's original enqueue time, so give it a longer retention than its source. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

visibilityTimeout.title: Visibility timeout
visibilityTimeout.description: A delivered message stays hidden this long. If it isn't deleted in time it is delivered again. AWS suggests at least six times a Lambda consumer's timeout (plus its batching window). A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

delay.title: Delivery delay
delay.description: New messages stay invisible this long (a delay queue). Per-message timers aren't modelled. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

maxReceives.title: Max receives
maxReceives.description: With a dead-letter queue connected: after this many deliveries without a delete, the message moves there. Without one, messages are retried until retention ends. AWS recommends at least 5 for a Lambda consumer. A hard limit of the provider.

inFlightLimit.title: In-flight limit
inFlightLimit.description: Messages delivered but not yet deleted. At the limit, consumers receive nothing until it drops. About 120,000 for a standard queue (raisable); AWS says a FIFO queue's depends on its active message groups and is also 120,000 by default. In messages. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

highThroughput.title: FIFO high throughput
highThroughput.description: FIFO only. Raises the rate limit to the region's high-throughput quota (set in the account quotas). A single message group is still held to one partition's 300 calls a second.

deduplication.title: FIFO deduplication
deduplication.description: FIFO only. A message whose id was accepted in the last five minutes is acknowledged but not enqueued again, which is what a producer retrying a send with the same deduplication id gets. The sender's message id is the deduplication id: two different messages with identical bodies can't be told apart, so content-based deduplication isn't modelled.

redrive.title: Redrive messages
redrive.description: Moves this queue's waiting messages to the queue on its 'redrive' port, oldest first, at the velocity below, until switched off. This is DLQ redrive: the messages become new messages in the destination with a fresh retention clock.

redriveVelocity.title: Redrive velocity
redriveVelocity.description: Messages moved per second. 0 is 'system optimised', which AWS describes as the maximum and gives no number for: 1,000 a second is assumed. In messages/s. A hard limit of the provider.

aws.sns.settings.description: Settings of SNS topic: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: FIFO keeps the order of each message group and can deduplicate, and is limited to 300 messages a second per group. Its subscribers must be SQS queues. One of: standard (Standard), fifo (FIFO).

maxMessageSize.title: Maximum message size
maxMessageSize.description: 256 KB by default; a topic can raise it to 1 MiB (the `MaximumMessageSize` attribute), which AWS only allows with 100 subscriptions or fewer. The size counts the body and the attributes of a publish, or of a whole batch. In KB. A hard limit of the provider.

publishLatency.title: Publish latency
publishLatency.description: How long a publish takes to be acknowledged. AWS publishes no figure; an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

deliveryLatency.title: Delivery latency
deliveryLatency.description: Time between a publish being accepted and SNS handing the message to a subscriber. AWS publishes no figure; an assumption, and 0 so that deliveries start at once. On a FIFO topic it is spent inside the message group, so it also limits how fast a group can go.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

fifoThroughput.title: Fifo throughput
fifoThroughput.description: FIFO only (the FifoThroughputScope attribute). Topic scope: the topic as a whole is limited to 3,000 messages or 20 MB a second, and deduplicates across the topic. Message group scope lifts the topic limit to the region's publish quota, with deduplication per group. A group always stays at 300 a second. AWS does not let a topic go back to Topic scope once it has been changed. One of: topic (Topic (default)), messageGroup (Message group (high throughput)).

deduplication.title: FIFO deduplication
deduplication.description: FIFO only. A publish whose message was already accepted in the last five minutes (a publisher retrying after a timeout) is acknowledged but not delivered again. Real FIFO topics always deduplicate; this is off by default because it costs memory proportional to the publish rate over five minutes.

maxPendingPerSubscription.title: Pending deliveries per subscription
maxPendingPerSubscription.description: SNS keeps retrying a message for up to 23 days; the simulator has to bound what it remembers. Deliveries waiting on a subscriber (retrying, queued behind a FIFO group or a throttle) beyond this are dropped and counted as overflow. An assumption: AWS publishes no such limit. In messages.

aws.kinesis.settings.description: Settings of Kinesis data stream: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

mode.title: Capacity mode
mode.description: Provisioned: you choose the shards, each 1 MiB/s and 1,000 records/s in, 2 MiB/s out. On-demand: starts at four shards (4 MB/s) and splits any shard taking more than 500 KB/s, so it holds about twice its peak; traffic that more than doubles faster than it splits is throttled. Switching keeps the shards there are. One of: provisioned (Provisioned), on-demand (On-demand).

shards.title: Shards
shards.description: Provisioned mode. Changing it while running is UpdateShardCount: uniform scaling, at most double or half the current count per step (a few minutes each, assumed 2), ten steps in 24 hours. Old shards close and are read to their end before their children. In shards. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

retention.title: Retention
retention.description: How long records stay readable. A consumer blocked by a failing batch, or simply behind, loses what is older than this. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

maxRecordSize.title: Maximum record size
maxRecordSize.description: Records up to this size are accepted (1 MiB by default, up to 10 MiB). A large record draws on the shard's burst and can throttle the writes behind it. In KiB. A hard limit of the provider.

splitDelay.title: On-demand split delay
splitDelay.description: How long after a shard goes over 500 KB/s (or 500 records/s) on-demand splits it. AWS says it splits "within 15 minutes" and that traffic more than doubling inside 15 minutes can be throttled; the bound is used. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

aws.firehose.settings.description: Settings of Firehose stream: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

destination.title: Destination
destination.description: What the 'out' port is. Amazon S3: one object per buffer, retried for 24 hours (or as long as a source stream keeps the records). HTTP endpoint (or a partner such as Datadog or Splunk): one request per buffer, retried for the retry duration, then backed up to the S3 bucket on the 'backup' port. One of: s3 (Amazon S3), http (HTTP endpoint).

bufferSize.title: Buffer size
bufferSize.description: Deliver once this much has gathered, or when the interval is up, whichever comes first. A hint: Firehose grows the buffer when delivery falls behind. HTTP endpoints take at most 64 MiB. With a Kinesis source each shard has its own buffer. In MiB. A hard limit of the provider.

bufferInterval.title: Buffer interval
bufferInterval.description: Deliver what has gathered this long after the first record of a buffer arrived. 0 delivers within a few seconds (once a second is assumed). AWS's default is 300 s for S3 and 60 s for an HTTP endpoint. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

retryDuration.title: Retry duration (HTTP endpoint)
retryDuration.description: How long a failing delivery to an HTTP endpoint is retried before the data is backed up to S3. 0 doesn't retry. S3 destinations ignore it: they retry for 24 hours. AWS gives no default for HTTP endpoints; 300 s is its OpenSearch default. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

transform.title: Transformation
transform.description: Used when a Lambda function is wired to the 'transform' port.

bufferSize.title: Buffer size
bufferSize.description: Records are sent to the transformation Lambda in batches of about this much. In MB. A hard limit of the provider.

bufferInterval.title: Buffer interval
bufferInterval.description: Or after this long, whichever comes first. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

retries.title: Retries
retries.description: Retries of a failed invocation (a timeout, a throttle, an error) before its records are treated as failed and written to the error prefix. AWS's default is 3; it publishes no maximum (10 here).

outputRatio.title: Output size ratio
outputRatio.description: Bytes the function returns per byte it is given (compacting or enriching the records). An assumption about your function.

aws.eventbridge.settings.description: Settings of EventBridge event bus: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

putLatency.title: PutEvents latency
putLatency.description: How long a PutEvents request takes to be answered. AWS publishes no figure; an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

deliveryLatency.title: Delivery latency
deliveryLatency.description: From an event being accepted to the first attempt to invoke a target (IngestionToInvocationStartLatency). AWS reported a P99 of 129 ms in 2024; the shape is an assumption with a P99 of about 125 ms.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

initial.title: First backoff
initial.description: The longest wait before the first retry; each wait is drawn between zero and its limit (full jitter). An assumption: AWS publishes no delays. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

max.title: Longest backoff
max.description: The limit doubles after each retry up to this. An assumption, chosen so that 185 retries take about 24 hours, as AWS's default policy does. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

maxPendingPerTarget.title: Pending deliveries per target
maxPendingPerTarget.description: EventBridge keeps retrying an event for up to 24 hours; the simulator has to bound what it remembers. Deliveries waiting on a target (delayed or retrying) beyond this are dropped and counted as overflow. An assumption: AWS publishes no such limit. In events.

aws.scheduler.settings.description: Settings of EventBridge Scheduler: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: The schedule's state. A disabled schedule invokes nothing new; invocations already created carry on.

expression.title: Schedule expression
expression.description: rate(5 minutes), rate(1 hour); cron(minutes hours day-of-month month day-of-week year), e.g. cron(0 0 * * ? *) for midnight every day; or at(2026-01-06T00:00:00) for once. Cron and at are read on the clock below.

clock.title: Clock at the start
clock.description: The time on the schedule's clock (in its time zone) when the simulation starts, so a cron or at expression knows when it is. The default is five minutes before midnight on a Monday. Daylight saving changes are not modelled.

schedules.title: Schedules
schedules.description: How many schedules share this expression and target: one per tenant, say. They come due together and each is invoked at its own moment in the window, so many schedules make a burst. In schedules.

flexibleWindow.title: Flexible time window
flexibleWindow.description: 0 is OFF: invocations land within the minute they are due. Otherwise each invocation lands at a random moment up to this many minutes after it is due, which spreads a crowd of schedules out. In min. A hard limit of the provider.

payload.title: Input size
payload.description: Size of the Input each invocation delivers to the target. In KB. A hard limit of the provider.

maxRetries.title: Maximum retries
maxRetries.description: Retries after the first attempt (MaximumRetryAttempts). 0 tries once. A hard limit of the provider.

maxEventAge.title: Maximum event age
maxEventAge.description: Stop retrying once the event is this old (MaximumEventAgeInSeconds), counted from when it was accepted. Time spent delayed by a rate limit counts too. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

initial.title: First backoff
initial.description: The longest wait before the first retry; each wait is drawn between zero and its limit (full jitter). An assumption: AWS publishes no delays. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

max.title: Longest backoff
max.description: The limit doubles after each retry up to this. An assumption, chosen so that 185 retries take about 24 hours, as AWS's default policy does. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

maxPending.title: Pending invocations
maxPending.description: Scheduler keeps retrying for up to 24 hours; the simulator has to bound what it remembers. Invocations waiting on the target (delayed or retrying) beyond this are dropped and counted as overflow. An assumption: AWS publishes no such limit. In invocations.

aws.stepfunctions.settings.description: Settings of Step Functions state machine: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

workflowType.title: Type
workflowType.description: Standard: exactly-once, up to a year, StartExecution answered at once, state transitions throttled by the account's quota, a 25,000-event history. Express: at-least-once (asynchronous) or at-most-once (synchronous), up to five minutes, a much higher start rate, no transition quota. A synchronous caller waits for an Express execution's result (StartSyncExecution); a Standard one is answered at once. AWS doesn't let a state machine change type. One of: standard (Standard), express (Express).

timeout.title: Execution timeout (TimeoutSeconds)
timeout.description: The state machine's TimeoutSeconds: an execution still running this long fails with States.Timeout. 0 for none, which leaves the type's own maximum: a year (Standard) or five minutes (Express), whichever is shorter applies. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

afterCatch.title: Fallback path ends in
afterCatch.description: Where the states on the catch port lead: a saga usually ends in a Fail state once it has compensated, so the execution still counts (and answers) as failed. One of: fail (A Fail state), succeed (A Succeed state).

startLatency.title: StartExecution response time
startLatency.description: How long StartExecution takes to answer with the new execution's ARN (Standard, and asynchronous Express). A synchronous Express caller hears when the execution ends instead. AWS publishes no figure; an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

transitionLatency.title: State transition time
transitionLatency.description: How long Step Functions takes to move into a state, on top of what the state does. AWS publishes no figure; an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

duplicateRate.title: Duplicate executions (asynchronous Express)
duplicateRate.description: Asynchronous Express workflows are at-least-once: an execution may run more than once. The share of them that do (each runs exactly twice here). AWS publishes no rate, so 0 by default; raise it to see what a task that isn't idempotent does. Standard (exactly-once) and synchronous Express (at-most-once) never duplicate. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

aws.dynamodb.settings.description: Settings of DynamoDB table: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

readCapacity.title: Provisioned read capacity
readCapacity.description: Provisioned mode. Capped by the per-table and per-account quotas. In RCU. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

writeCapacity.title: Provisioned write capacity
writeCapacity.description: In WCU. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

partitions.title: Partitions
partitions.description: 0 derives it from capacity. AWS doesn't publish how many partitions a table has or when it splits, so this is a modelling choice.

readConsistency.title: Read consistency
readConsistency.description: Eventually consistent reads cost half a unit per 4 KB, strongly consistent one, transactional two. One of: eventual (Eventual), strong (Strong), transactional (Transactional).

writeMode.title: Write mode
writeMode.description: Transactional writes cost twice as much, and a transaction holds at most 100 items and 4 MB. One of: standard (Standard), transactional (Transactional).

burstSeconds.title: Burst capacity
burstSeconds.description: Seconds of unused capacity banked for bursts. AWS retains up to 300 s and says this may change; how it refills is not published. In s. A hard limit of the provider.

latency.title: Request latency
latency.description: AWS says 'single-digit milliseconds' and publishes no percentiles; an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

conditionFailureRate.title: Condition failure rate
conditionFailureRate.description: Share of writes whose condition expression is false. AWS still charges the write capacity; nothing changes (no index or stream write) and the call fails with ConditionalCheckFailedException, which retrying cannot fix. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

maxReadUnits.title: Maximum read throughput
maxReadUnits.description: On-demand only. Throttles reads above this with ThrottlingException. 0 is no maximum (the per-table quota applies). AWS applies it best effort and burst capacity can exceed it briefly. In RRU/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

maxWriteUnits.title: Maximum write throughput
maxWriteUnits.description: On-demand only. Throttles writes above this with ThrottlingException. 0 is no maximum. In WRU/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

warmReadUnits.title: Pre-warmed reads
warmReadUnits.description: Warm throughput raised ahead of a launch: reads per second the table absorbs instantly. 0 keeps AWS's default for a new table (12,000). Capped by the per-table quota. In RRU/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

warmWriteUnits.title: Pre-warmed writes
warmWriteUnits.description: Warm throughput for writes. 0 keeps AWS's default for a new table (4,000). In WRU/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

scaleInterval.title: Scale-out interval
scaleInterval.description: How long DynamoDB needs to double the capacity a table can absorb beyond twice its previous peak. AWS says throttling can occur if you exceed double your previous peak within 30 minutes; it does not publish a fixed step, so treat this as the documented guidance. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

count.title: Global secondary indexes
count.description: How many GSIs the table has (all alike). Capped by the per-table index quota (20). Each write to the table also writes to every index and is throttled if any index can't absorb it. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

readCapacity.title: Read capacity per index
readCapacity.description: Provisioned mode: each index has its own capacity. 0 gives each index the table's read capacity. In RCU. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

writeCapacity.title: Write capacity per index
writeCapacity.description: Provisioned mode: each index has its own capacity, and AWS advises at least the table's. Below it, the table is throttled. 0 gives each index the table's write capacity. In WCU. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

maxReadUnits.title: Maximum read throughput per index
maxReadUnits.description: On-demand only. 0 is no maximum. In RRU/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

maxWriteUnits.title: Maximum write throughput per index
maxWriteUnits.description: On-demand only. 0 is no maximum. In WRU/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

entryBytes.title: Index entry size
entryBytes.description: What one index entry weighs: 0 projects the whole item (ALL). For KEYS_ONLY or INCLUDE give the size of the keys plus projected attributes. Write units are charged per KB of it, read units per 4 KB. In bytes.

writeShare.title: Writes that touch an index
writeShare.description: Share of table writes that add, change or remove an entry in each index. A write that leaves the index key and projected attributes alone, or an item without the index key (a sparse index), costs the index nothing. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

keyChangeShare.title: Writes that change the index key
keyChangeShare.description: Share of indexed writes that move an entry (change the index key). AWS charges two index writes for them: one delete and one put. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

readShare.title: Reads that query an index
readShare.description: Share of reads that are Queries on an index instead of the table. They use the index's read capacity, are always eventually consistent, and are spread over the indexes evenly. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

keyValues.title: Distinct index key values
keyValues.description: 0 spreads index entries the way the table's keys are spread. A small number (a 'status' key with 3 values) concentrates them on that many index partitions, which throttle at 1,000 writes a second each and push back on the table. A hot table key stays hot on the index.

count.title: Local secondary indexes
count.description: Up to 5, fixed at table creation. They share the table's capacity: each write also costs the table the index writes. The 10 GB item collection limit is documentation only here. A hard limit of the provider.

entryBytes.title: Index entry size
entryBytes.description: 0 projects the whole item (ALL). Otherwise the size of the keys plus projected attributes. In bytes.

writeShare.title: Writes that touch an index
writeShare.description: Share of table writes that add, change or remove an entry in each local index. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

expiresPerSecond.title: Items expiring per second
expiresPerSecond.description: Items deleted by Time to Live. They use no write capacity on the table (AWS), but are removed from every index (index write capacity), appear in the stream, and replicate to replicas, which pay for them. AWS deletes 'within a few days' of expiry; here it is the steady rate. In items/s.

itemBytes.title: Expiring item size
itemBytes.description: Assumed average size of an expiring item, which sets the size of its stream record and index writes. In bytes.

view.title: View
view.description: What a stream record carries (StreamViewType). Records are produced while consumers are wired to the stream port and this isn't off; it sets the record's size. One of: off (Off), keys (Keys only), new (New image), old (Old image), new-and-old (New and old images).

propagation.title: Stream delay
propagation.description: From a write returning to its stream record being readable. AWS says 'near-real time' and publishes no figure; an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

replication.title: Global tables
replication.description: Applies when replicas are wired to the replicas port.

lag.title: Replication lag
lag.description: From a write to it reaching a replica, on top of the edge's network latency. AWS says typically a second or less; the distribution is an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

aws.rds.settings.description: Settings of RDS database: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

engine.title: Engine
engine.description: Decides the default max_connections formula, the errors clients see, and whether this is an RDS instance (storage with IOPS, Multi-AZ standbys, read replicas) or an Aurora cluster (a shared cluster volume, a writer and up to 15 readers). One of: postgres (RDS for PostgreSQL), mysql (RDS for MySQL), mariadb (RDS for MariaDB), aurora-postgres (Aurora PostgreSQL), aurora-mysql (Aurora MySQL).

instanceClass.title: Instance class
instanceClass.description: vCPUs and memory, from AWS's hardware table. Memory sets the default max_connections; vCPUs set how much query work runs at once. Readers use the same class. One of: db.t3.micro (Db.t3.micro), db.t3.medium (Db.t3.medium), db.t4g.micro (Db.t4g.micro), db.t4g.medium (Db.t4g.medium), db.t4g.large (Db.t4g.large), db.m5.large (Db.m5.large), db.m6g.large (Db.m6g.large), db.m6gd.large (Db.m6gd.large), db.m6gd.xlarge (Db.m6gd.xlarge), db.m7g.large (Db.m7g.large), db.m7g.xlarge (Db.m7g.xlarge), db.m7g.2xlarge (Db.m7g.2xlarge), db.m7g.4xlarge (Db.m7g.4xlarge), db.r6g.large (Db.r6g.large), db.r6g.xlarge (Db.r6g.xlarge), db.r6gd.large (Db.r6gd.large), db.r6gd.xlarge (Db.r6gd.xlarge), db.r6gd.2xlarge (Db.r6gd.2xlarge), db.r7g.large (Db.r7g.large), db.r7g.xlarge (Db.r7g.xlarge), db.r7g.2xlarge (Db.r7g.2xlarge), db.r7g.4xlarge (Db.r7g.4xlarge), db.r7g.8xlarge (Db.r7g.8xlarge), db.r7g.16xlarge (Db.r7g.16xlarge).

maxConnections.title: max_connections
maxConnections.description: 0 keeps the default parameter group's value, derived from the class's memory (MySQL: memory/12,582,880; MariaDB: memory/25,165,760 up to 12,000; PostgreSQL: memory/9,531,392 up to 5,000; Aurora MySQL: AWS's table). Each instance has its own. A hard limit of the provider.

multiAz.title: Multi az
multiAz.description: RDS engines only. A Multi-AZ DB instance keeps a synchronous standby in another Availability Zone that serves nothing until it takes over; a Multi-AZ DB cluster has two standbys, in two other zones, that serve reads too. Aurora's availability comes from its readers instead, spread over the zones after the writer's. One of: none (Single-AZ), instance (Multi-AZ DB instance (one standby)), cluster (Multi-AZ DB cluster (two readable standbys)).

readers.title: Readers
readers.description: Aurora Replicas behind the reader endpoint (failover targets), or RDS read replicas (asynchronous copies, not failover targets). Same class as the writer. Reads go to them when the client's endpoint says so. A hard limit of the provider.

query.title: Queries
query.description: A call is one query (a batch of n records, n of them, on one connection).

readCpu.title: Read: vCPU time
readCpu.description: vCPU time one read needs. Queries queue for a vCPU when every one is busy, which is how query time stretches as the CPU saturates. An assumption: it depends on your queries.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

readWait.title: Read: other time
readWait.description: Time a read spends off the CPU at low load: buffer pool misses, storage, locks. An assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

writeCpu.title: Write: vCPU time
writeCpu.description: vCPU time one write needs. An assumption.

writeWait.title: Write: other time
writeWait.description: Time a write spends off the CPU at low load: the log flush, storage, row locks. An assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

readIos.title: Storage I/Os per read
readIos.description: Reads served from the buffer pool cost none. An assumption. Past the volume's IOPS they queue (RDS storage only).

writeIos.title: Storage I/Os per write
writeIos.description: Data and log pages written. An assumption.

handshake.title: Handshake
handshake.description: Opening a connection: TCP, TLS and authentication round trips, paid by every request that has no open connection to reuse. AWS publishes no figure; an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

cpu.title: Server CPU per new connection
cpu.description: vCPU time the database spends accepting a connection (TLS, authentication, a backend process). A storm of new connections competes with queries for the vCPUs. An assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

type.title: Type
type.description: RDS engines only: Aurora's cluster volume isn't provisioned by IOPS, and isn't limited here. One of: gp3 (General Purpose (gp3)), io1 (Provisioned IOPS (io1)), io2 (Provisioned IOPS (io2 Block Express)).

allocated.title: Allocated storage
allocated.description: gp3's baseline jumps from 3,000 to 12,000 IOPS at 400 GiB, where RDS stripes it over four volumes. io1 and io2 need 100 GiB or more. In GiB. A hard limit of the provider.

iops.title: Provisioned IOPS
iops.description: 0 is gp3's baseline (or io1/io2's 1,000 minimum). gp3 can be provisioned 12,000–64,000 from 400 GiB; io1 1,000–256,000 at up to 50 per GiB; io2 1,000–256,000 at up to 1,000 per GiB. Out-of-range values are clamped (the audit says so). In IOPS. A hard limit of the provider.

standbyCommit.title: Standby commit
standbyCommit.description: Multi-AZ (RDS): what a write waits for the standby to acknowledge. AWS says synchronous replication increases write and commit latency but gives no figure; an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

replicaLag.title: Replica lag
replicaLag.description: From a write on the writer to readers seeing it, recorded per write. Aurora: 'usually much less than 100 milliseconds'. RDS read replicas replicate asynchronously with the engine's own replication, typically slower and worse under heavy writes; raise it for them. An assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

failover.title: Failover
failover.description: An Outage on this node is its primary failing, and an Outage on its primary's Availability Zone loses the primary with the zone. The database is then unavailable for its failover time while a standby or reader in another zone takes over (an Outage on the node itself keeps it down for the outage, if that is longer), every connection to the old primary is dropped, and clients reconnect. With nothing in another zone to take over, a zone outage keeps the database down until the zone returns.

multiAzInstance.title: Multi-AZ DB instance
