aws.rds-proxy.settings.description: Settings of RDS Proxy: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

maxConnectionsPercent.title: Connection pool maximum connections
maxConnectionsPercent.description: MaxConnectionsPercent: the most database connections the proxy opens, as a share of the database's max_connections. Set it below 100 to leave room for other clients of the database. AWS recommends at least 20 (30 on a db.t3.small). In %. A hard limit of the provider.

maxIdleConnectionsPercent.title: Maximum idle connections
maxIdleConnectionsPercent.description: MaxIdleConnectionsPercent: database connections the proxy keeps open while idle, as a share of max_connections; beyond it, connections idle for five minutes are closed. At most MaxConnectionsPercent (clamped). AWS's default is half of MaxConnectionsPercent: 50 here. In %. A hard limit of the provider.

borrowTimeout.title: Connection borrow timeout
borrowTimeout.description: How long a request waits for a database connection when the pool is at its maximum and all are busy, or while the database fails over, before it gets 'Timed-out waiting to acquire database connection'. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

idleClientTimeout.title: Idle client connection timeout
idleClientTimeout.description: The proxy closes a client connection idle this long. Default 1,800 seconds. AWS states no range; the proxy ends every client connection after 24 hours, so that is the maximum here. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.description: The proxy endpoint its clients use: the default one reaches the writer; a read-only endpoint reaches an Aurora cluster's readers. One of: read-write (Read/write (the writer)), read-only (Read-only (the readers)).

pinning.title: Pinned sessions
pinning.description: Share of client sessions that do something the proxy can't multiplex (session variables, prepared statements, temporary tables, a statement over 16 KB). A pinned session keeps its database connection until the client connection closes, so a client that keeps connections open ties up one database connection each. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

latency.title: Proxy latency
latency.description: What the proxy's hop adds to each request, on top of the network. AWS publishes no figure; an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

clientHandshake.title: Client handshake
clientHandshake.description: Opening a client connection to the proxy: TLS and authentication, which the proxy handles instead of the database. An assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

targetCheck.title: Target check interval
targetCheck.description: While the database is unavailable (failing over), how often the proxy tries it again; requests wait meanwhile. AWS says the proxy monitors its targets actively but not how often; an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

aws.elasticache.settings.description: Settings of ElastiCache cluster: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

engine.title: Engine
engine.description: Valkey and Redis OSS execute commands on one main thread and replicate; Memcached is multi-threaded, has no replicas and no failover, and evicts least recently used items whatever their TTL. One of: valkey (Valkey), redis (Redis OSS), memcached (Memcached).

deployment.title: Deployment
deployment.description: A node-based cluster has the node type, shards and replicas below. Serverless has none of them: it is billed and throttled in ECPUs, starts at 30,000 a second and doubles every few minutes under load (see Serverless). One of: node-based (Node-based cluster), serverless (Serverless).

nodeType.title: Node type
nodeType.description: Memory, network bandwidth and vCPUs come from AWS's tables. How many commands a second a node executes is an assumption (see Performance). One of: cache.t4g.micro (cache.t4g.micro (0.5 GiB, 2 vCPU, 0.064 Gbps)), cache.t4g.small (cache.t4g.small (1.37 GiB, 2 vCPU, 0.128 Gbps)), cache.t4g.medium (cache.t4g.medium (3.09 GiB, 2 vCPU, 0.256 Gbps)), cache.m7g.large (cache.m7g.large (6.38 GiB, 2 vCPU, 0.937 Gbps)), cache.m7g.xlarge (cache.m7g.xlarge (12.93 GiB, 4 vCPU, 1.876 Gbps)), cache.r6g.large (cache.r6g.large (13.07 GiB, 2 vCPU, 0.75 Gbps)), cache.r7g.large (cache.r7g.large (13.07 GiB, 2 vCPU, 0.937 Gbps)), cache.r7g.xlarge (cache.r7g.xlarge (26.32 GiB, 4 vCPU, 1.876 Gbps)), cache.r7g.2xlarge (cache.r7g.2xlarge (52.82 GiB, 8 vCPU, 3.75 Gbps)), cache.r7g.4xlarge (cache.r7g.4xlarge (105.81 GiB, 16 vCPU, 7.5 Gbps)), cache.c7gn.large (cache.c7gn.large (3.09 GiB, 2 vCPU, 6.25 Gbps)).

clusterMode.title: Cluster mode
clusterMode.description: Valkey and Redis OSS only. Off: one shard (a primary and its replicas), scaled up by node type. On: keys hash to 16,384 slots spread over the shards, so the data and the load are split, and a hot key loads one shard. Automatic failover is always on in cluster mode.

shards.title: Shards (nodes for Memcached)
shards.description: Node groups, each with its own slots, memory and primary. Used when cluster mode is on, or as the node count of a Memcached cluster. The account's nodes-per-cluster quota (90 by default) caps shards x (1 + replicas). A hard limit of the provider.

replicasPerShard.title: Replicas per shard
replicasPerShard.description: Read-only copies of each shard's primary, each in another Availability Zone (Multi-AZ). They serve reads when reads go to replicas, apply every write the primary takes, and one is promoted when the primary, or its zone, fails. Memcached has none. A hard limit of the provider.

readFrom.title: Read from
readFrom.description: Where the client sends reads: the reader endpoint or READONLY connections send them to replicas. Writes and fills always go to the primary. One of: primary (Primary only), replicas (Replicas (primary if none is up)), any (Any node of the shard).

automaticFailover.title: Multi-AZ automatic failover
automaticFailover.description: When a primary fails, promote a replica within the detection and promotion time. Off (cluster mode off only): the primary is replaced, which takes the replacement time, and with no replica its data is lost.

keys.title: Distinct keys
keys.description: How many different keys the application reads and writes. Requests pick one by their key, so few keys means a high hit ratio and many a low one. A property of your application.

popularitySkew.title: Popularity skew
popularitySkew.description: 1 spreads requests evenly over the keys. Higher values concentrate them on a few (a long tail): key i of N is chosen with probability rising as (i / N)^(1 / skew).

itemSize.title: Value size
itemSize.description: The average value. It decides how many keys fit in memory, the bytes a node sends (its network bandwidth is a limit) and, on serverless, the ECPUs a command costs. In KB. A hard limit of the provider.

ttl.title: TTL
ttl.description: How long a filled key lives. 0: keys never expire (and volatile-lru then has nothing it may evict). A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

ttlJitter.title: TTL jitter
ttlJitter.description: Shorten each key's TTL by a random share of up to this much, so keys filled together (after a cold start) do not all expire together. AWS's caching best practices suggest it against the thundering herd. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

writes.title: Writes
writes.description: What the application does to the cache after a write to the database. Write-through keeps written keys hot, and fills memory with keys that may never be read. One of: invalidate (Invalidate (DEL after the database write)), write-through (Write-through (SET after the database write)).

stampede.title: Stampede
stampede.description: What the application does when many requests miss the same key at once. Plain cache-aside sends every one of them to the database (the thundering herd). A lock (SET NX) lets one fetch while the rest wait for its fill. One of: none (None: every miss reads the database), lock (Lock: one reader per key fills it, the others wait).

failOpen.title: Fail open
failOpen.description: When the cache cannot answer (a shard failing over, a node refusing connections), read from the database instead, and treat a failed cache update after a write as harmless. Off: those requests fail.

reservedMemoryPercent.title: reserved-memory-percent
reservedMemoryPercent.description: Share of maxmemory set aside for replication buffers, fragmentation and forks. AWS's default is 25% and advises not to lower it. Valkey and Redis OSS only. In %.

evictionPolicy.title: Eviction policy
evictionPolicy.description: maxmemory-policy when memory is full. volatile-lru (AWS's default) evicts only keys with a TTL; allkeys-lru any key; noeviction none. When nothing may be evicted a SET fails with OOM. Memcached always evicts the least recently used. One of: volatile-lru (Volatile lru), allkeys-lru (Allkeys lru), noeviction (Noeviction).

keyOverhead.title: Overhead per key
keyOverhead.description: Memory a key costs besides its value: the key name, the dictionary entry and the expiry. An assumption; it depends on your key names. In bytes.

memcachedMaxItemSize.title: Memcached max_item_size
memcachedMaxItemSize.description: Memcached refuses to store a larger value, so every read of it misses. AWS's default is 1 MB; the upper bound here is an assumption. In KB.

opsPerNode.title: Commands per second per node
opsPerNode.description: How many simple GET/SET commands one node executes a second. 0 uses the node type's figure (100,000 to 1,000,000, Memcached 100,000 per vCPU). AWS publishes none except 'over 1 million requests per second per node' on r7g.4xlarge and larger, so these are assumptions. In ops/s.

detection.title: Failure detection
detection.description: How long before ElastiCache notices a failed primary. AWS publishes no figure: an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

promotion.title: Replica promotion
promotion.description: From detection until the promoted replica takes writes. AWS says 'typically just a few seconds'; the figure is an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

replacement.title: Node replacement
replacement.description: How long provisioning a replacement node takes: a failed primary without automatic failover, a Memcached node, or the replica that replaces a promoted one. AWS publishes no figure: an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

replicaResync.title: Replica resync
replicaResync.description: After a promotion the other replicas drop their data and sync from the new primary, and cannot be read meanwhile. AWS says it is a brief interruption; the length is an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

maxEcpuPerSecond.title: Maximum ECPU per second
maxEcpuPerSecond.description: A cost cap: over it ElastiCache throttles requests. 0 for none. In ECPU/s.

minEcpuPerSecond.title: Minimum ECPU per second (pre-scaling)
minEcpuPerSecond.description: Throughput the cache is ready for from the start, instead of 30,000 a second. AWS takes up to an hour to apply it; here it applies at once. In ECPU/s.

maxStorageGb.title: Maximum data storage
maxStorageGb.description: A cost cap: at it ElastiCache evicts keys with a TTL (least recently used first) and, with none to evict, fails writes with OOM. 0 for none. The upper bound here is a UI bound, not AWS's. In GB.

scaleInterval.title: Doubling time
scaleInterval.description: How often the throughput the cache supports may double while traffic presses on it. AWS says every 2 to 3 minutes (Valkey 8); 150 s is the middle. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

latency.title: Command latency
latency.description: What a command takes through the serverless proxy layer. AWS says sub-millisecond at the median; the distribution is an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

failShard.title: Shard to fail
failShard.description: Which shard's primary (Memcached: which node) fails when you press Fail primary.

failPrimary.title: Fail primary now
failPrimary.description: Change this number while running (or in a scenario's timeline) to fail the primary of the shard above, as an instance failure or the TestFailover API would. To lose every node in an Availability Zone, inject an Outage on the zone instead.

flush.title: Flush now
flush.description: Change this number while running to empty every node (FLUSHALL, a reboot, or a cluster that came back empty): the next requests all miss.

aws.opensearch.settings.description: Settings of OpenSearch domain: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

instanceType.title: Data node type
instanceType.description: Each data node's vCPUs size its thread pools (write: one per vCPU; search: 1.5 per vCPU + 1) and share their CPU; its memory sets the Java heap (half, at most 32 GiB), which sets the indexing pressure limit. Larger types also accept larger requests (10 MiB or 100 MiB). One of: t3.medium.search (T3.medium.search), m6g.large.search (M6g.large.search), m6g.xlarge.search (M6g.xlarge.search), m6g.2xlarge.search (M6g.2xlarge.search), c6g.xlarge.search (C6g.xlarge.search), c6g.2xlarge.search (C6g.2xlarge.search), r6g.large.search (R6g.large.search), r6g.xlarge.search (R6g.xlarge.search), r6g.2xlarge.search (R6g.2xlarge.search), r6g.4xlarge.search (R6g.4xlarge.search), r7g.large.search (R7g.large.search), r7g.xlarge.search (R7g.xlarge.search), r7g.2xlarge.search (R7g.2xlarge.search), r7g.4xlarge.search (R7g.4xlarge.search).

dataNodes.title: Data nodes
dataNodes.description: AWS recommends at least three. The per-domain instance quota is an account quota (default 200); AWS raises it to at most 1,002. In nodes. A hard limit of the provider.

availabilityZones.title: Availability Zones
availabilityZones.description: 1: every data node in one zone (zone awareness off, the API's default), so losing that zone loses the domain. 2 or 3 (Multi-AZ without Standby): data nodes are spread over that many zones, from the node's own zone (or the region's first), and the copies of each shard are put in different zones, so with replicas a zone outage leaves a copy of every shard (yellow) and the domain carries on. AWS recommends 3 zones and a node count that is a multiple of them. In zones. A hard limit of the provider.

primaryShards.title: Primary shards
primaryShards.description: Shards of the index. OpenSearch Service creates an index with 5 by default (open-source OpenSearch: 1). Fixed when the index is created; here a change re-places the shards at once. Use a multiple of the data node count to spread them evenly. In shards. A hard limit of the provider.

replicas.title: Replicas
replicas.description: Copies of each primary shard, each on a different node. Every indexed document is written again on each replica (write capacity), and a search can use any copy. With none, a failed node takes its shards' data with it. More copies than nodes can't be placed (the cluster stays yellow). The maximum here is a bound for the form, not an OpenSearch limit. In per shard.

routing.title: Shard routing
routing.description: By document ID (OpenSearch's default) spreads a bulk request's documents over every shard, and a search asks every shard. By routing key, the message's key picks one shard for all of a request's documents and for its search: a tenant or user ID as custom routing. A hot key then makes a hot shard. One of: id (By document ID), key (By routing key).

refreshInterval.title: Refresh interval
refreshInterval.description: How often shards refresh, making what was indexed since searchable (index.refresh_interval, 1 s by default). 0 turns refresh off (OpenSearch's -1), as people do during a large reindex: nothing new becomes searchable until it is turned on again. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cpuPerDocument.title: CPU per document
cpuPerDocument.description: CPU time to index one document, on the primary and again on each replica. Depends on document size, mapping and analysers; an assumption, measure your own. In ms.

cpuPerRequest.title: CPU per shard request
cpuPerRequest.description: CPU time each shard-level indexing request costs on top of its documents (parsing, translog, coordination). It is why one bulk request of many documents is cheaper than many single ones. An assumption. In ms.

waitForRefresh.title: Wait for refresh
waitForRefresh.description: refresh=wait_for: a write is answered only once its documents are searchable, at the next refresh. Ignored while refresh is off.

timeout.title: Primary wait timeout
timeout.description: The bulk and index APIs' timeout: how long a write waits for its shard's primary when it has none (a failed node not yet replaced by a replica, or no replica at all) before failing with 503 UnavailableShardsException. OpenSearch's default is 1 minute. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cpuPerShard.title: CPU per shard query
cpuPerShard.description: CPU time one shard takes to answer a search (query and fetch). Depends entirely on the query and the data; an assumption. Heavy aggregations are a larger mean.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

allowPartialResults.title: Allow partial results
allowPartialResults.description: allow_partial_search_results (true by default): a search that some shards couldn't answer (rejected, or no copy left) still succeeds with what the others returned. Off, it fails instead.

failedNodes.title: Failed data nodes
failedNodes.description: How many data nodes are down (the first ones). Set it from a scenario's timeline and back to 0 to bring them back: their work is lost, primaries on them are replaced by replicas after the detection delay, and a shard with no copy left is unavailable. An Outage on one of the domain's Availability Zones fails that zone's nodes the same way; an Outage fault on this node takes the whole domain endpoint down instead. In nodes.

detection.title: Failure detection
detection.description: How long the cluster takes to notice a failed node and promote replicas of its primaries. OpenSearch removes a node at once when its connection drops, and after 3 failed checks 1 s apart, each waiting up to 10 s, when it stops answering: about 30 s. Writes to its primaries wait meanwhile; searches use other copies at once. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

aws.s3.settings.description: Settings of S3 bucket: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

bucketType.title: Bucket type
bucketType.description: A general purpose bucket limits each prefix to 3,500 writes and 5,500 reads a second. An S3 Express One Zone directory bucket supports 200,000 writes and 2,000,000 reads a second in all, whatever the keys, and answers in single-digit milliseconds. One of: general (General purpose), directory (Directory (S3 Express One Zone)).

prefixes.title: Key prefixes
prefixes.description: How many distinct prefixes the requests spread over. Each prefix gets its own 3,500 write and 5,500 read requests a second. A hot key always lands on one prefix. A directory bucket ignores it.

prefixScaling.title: Prefix scale-up
prefixScaling.description: Model S3's gradual scaling of a new or suddenly hot prefix.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: S3 scales a busy prefix above its guaranteed rate, gradually, and answers 503 Slow Down while it does. Off: a prefix is held at the guaranteed rate. On: a prefix that keeps being refused is split, doubling its rate.

splitAfter.title: Split after
splitAfter.description: How long a prefix must be refused without a break before S3 doubles its rate. AWS says the scaling is gradual and publishes no timing: this is an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

maxSplits.title: Largest number of splits
maxSplits.description: A prefix is never scaled past 2 to this power times its guaranteed rate. AWS publishes no ceiling: this is an assumption.

deleteShare.title: Writes that are deletes
deleteShare.description: Share of write calls that are DELETEs: no body, same per-prefix allowance as PUT, and an object-removed event instead of object-created. The engine only tells a call apart as read or write, so the mix is set here. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

copyShare.title: Writes that are copies
copyShare.description: Share of write calls that are server-side COPYs: no upload from the client, the bytes move inside S3 at the transfer rate. Counted after the deletes, so delete plus copy share should not exceed 1. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

headShare.title: Reads that are HEADs
headShare.description: Share of read calls that are HEAD requests: metadata only, no body, the same per-prefix read allowance as GET. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

listShare.title: Reads that are LISTs
listShare.description: Share of read calls that are LIST requests (ListObjectsV2): no object body, a slower first byte. AWS publishes no separate LIST rate, so a LIST draws on the read allowance (an assumption). Counted before the HEADs. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

readLatency.title: First-byte latency (read)
readLatency.description: Time until the first byte of a GET or HEAD. AWS says roughly 100 to 200 ms for consistent latency and tens of ms median; a spread of about that is an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

writeLatency.title: First-byte latency (write)
writeLatency.description: Time until S3 starts accepting the body of a PUT or answers a DELETE. An assumption: AWS publishes no figure.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

listLatency.title: First-byte latency (list)
listLatency.description: Time until a LIST answers. An assumption: AWS publishes no figure.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

directoryLatencyFactor.title: Directory bucket speed-up
directoryLatencyFactor.description: How many times faster a directory bucket answers than a general purpose bucket, applied to the first-byte latencies above. AWS says S3 Express One Zone is up to 10 times faster; the exact factor is an assumption.

transferRate.title: Transfer rate per connection
transferRate.description: How fast one connection moves bytes, so a large object takes bytes / rate longer. About 90 MB/s per connection is older AWS guidance and an assumption; AWS now says only to use many parallel connections, and an instance can reach 100 Gb/s (12,500 MB/s). In MB/s.

multipart.title: Multipart transfers
multipart.description: Large objects as parallel parts. Each part is a request on the prefix, and an upload adds two more (start and complete).

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Split a large object into parts moved over parallel connections (multipart upload, or byte-range GETs). Off: one connection moves the whole object, and a write over 5 GB is refused.

threshold.title: Switch above
threshold.description: Object size at which a transfer is split. The AWS CLI default is 8 MB (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/topic/s3-config.html). In MiB.

partSize.title: Part size
partSize.description: Size of each part: 5 MiB to 5 GiB. It is raised if the object would need more than 10,000 parts. The AWS CLI default is 8 MB. In MiB. A hard limit of the provider.

concurrency.title: Parallel connections
concurrency.description: How many parts move at once. The AWS CLI default is 10 (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/topic/s3-config.html); S3 limits no one's connections. In connections.

storageClass.title: Storage class of the objects
storageClass.description: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA and Glacier Instant Retrieval read in milliseconds, like Standard. Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive objects cannot be read until restored: a GET is refused with 403 InvalidObjectState. One of: standard (Standard), intelligent-tiering (Intelligent-Tiering), standard-ia (Standard-IA), one-zone-ia (One Zone-IA), glacier-instant (Glacier Instant Retrieval), glacier-flexible (Glacier Flexible Retrieval), deep-archive (Glacier Deep Archive).

restoredShare.title: Archived reads that hit restored objects
restoredShare.description: In an archive storage class, the share of GETs that find the object already restored (a restore keeps a temporary copy for the days you ask). Restore jobs themselves (minutes to 48 hours) are not simulated. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

versioning.title: Versioning
versioning.description: With versioning on, a DELETE writes a delete marker instead of removing the object. It still costs one write request; the marker count is reported but changes nothing else.

notificationDelay.title: Event notification delay
notificationDelay.description: AWS says events are typically delivered in seconds but can take a minute or longer. The distribution is an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

duplicateRate.title: Duplicate notifications
duplicateRate.description: Share of event notifications delivered twice. AWS designs for at-least-once delivery and publishes no duplicate rate, so it defaults to none: set it to see how consumers cope. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

replicationDelay.title: Replication delay
replicationDelay.description: Time from a write to its replica being written, for a bucket wired to a replication destination. S3 RTC replicates most objects in seconds and 99.9% within 15 minutes; without it AWS gives no figure (the table of options says 24 to 48 hours is not SLA backed). The distribution is an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

replicationTimeControl.title: Replication Time Control
replicationTimeControl.description: Replicate with S3 RTC. Its data rate is capped by the account's replication transfer quota (1 Gb/s by default), shared by every bucket in the region; beyond it replicas queue and lag grows.

aws.ses.settings.description: Settings of SES email: only the ones you change; the rest take their defaults.

call.title: Call
call.description: What each incoming call is. A send is one message to every recipient it carries, so its size is the message size. A bulk send is one message per recipient (up to 50 entries), so the size is divided between them. One of: send (SendEmail / SendRawEmail / SMTP), bulk (SendBulkEmail).

api.title: Api
api.description: Decides the largest message: 40 MB through the v2 API or SMTP, 10 MB through the v1 API (both after MIME encoding; hard limits, see the README). One of: v2 (SES v2 API or SMTP), v1 (SES v1 API).

batchSize.title: Recipients per call
batchSize.description: How many recipients one incoming message carries (a message the caller sends with a count above 1 multiplies it). SES refuses more than 50 recipients per message or per bulk call, and quotas are counted in recipients, so this is how to see both limits bite. In recipients.

sendLatency.title: API latency
sendLatency.description: How long SendEmail takes to answer once the request arrives. AWS publishes no figure; an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

verifiedShare.title: Verified recipients
verifiedShare.description: Only matters in the sandbox, where SES refuses a message unless every recipient is a verified address or the mailbox simulator. The share of recipients that are. Zero is a real application mailing real customers. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

recipients.title: Recipients
recipients.description: How the people you mail behave. These decide what happens to each message after SES accepts it.

hardBounceRate.title: Hard bounce rate
hardBounceRate.description: Share of new addresses that do not exist or permanently refuse mail. Counts toward the bounce rate AWS acts on. AWS asks senders to stay under 5% (it reviews the account at 5%) and suggests under 2%. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

complaintRate.title: Complaint rate
complaintRate.description: Share of delivered mail the recipient reports as spam. AWS places the account under review at 0.1%. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

deferredRate.title: Delivered late
deferredRate.description: Share of recipients whose mail server cannot take the message at first (mailbox full, busy server). SES keeps retrying and publishes a delivery delay event. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

deferralRecovery.title: Late mail that gets through
deferralRecovery.description: Share of delayed messages that are delivered on a later attempt. The rest are still failing when SES stops retrying and end as a soft (transient) bounce, which does not count toward the bounce rate. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

virusRate.title: Rejected (virus)
virusRate.description: Share of messages SES accepts but then rejects because it finds a virus. A Reject event, nothing is delivered. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

repeatShare.title: Repeat recipients
repeatShare.description: Share of sends to an address the account has mailed before. If that address hard-bounced or complained earlier, the suppression list stops the send; without it the address bounces or complains again. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

openRate.title: Open rate
openRate.description: Share of delivered mail that is opened. Only drawn when an event destination subscribes to Open. An assumption. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

clickRate.title: Click rate
clickRate.description: Share of delivered mail with a link clicked. Only drawn when an event destination subscribes to Click. An assumption. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

timing.title: Timing
timing.description: How long each step of a message's life takes (all assumptions; AWS publishes none of them).

delivery.title: Time to deliver
delivery.description: From SES accepting a message to the recipient's server answering (the delivery or bounce). AWS says the first attempt is usually within milliseconds; the server's answer adds time. An assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

retryDelay.title: Time to deliver late mail
retryDelay.description: How long a delayed message takes to get through on a retry. AWS does not publish SES's retry schedule; an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

retryWindow.title: Retry window
retryWindow.description: How long SES keeps retrying a delayed message before giving up with a soft bounce. A configuration set's MaxDeliverySeconds takes 5 to 840 minutes; its default is not documented, so the maximum is assumed. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

complaintDelay.title: Time to complaint
complaintDelay.description: How long after delivery a complaint reaches SES through a feedback loop. It takes however long the recipient takes to hit Report spam; an assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

engagementDelay.title: Time to open or click
engagementDelay.description: How long after delivery a message is opened or a link clicked. An assumption.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

enabled.title: Account-level suppression list
enabled.description: On by default for accounts created after 25 November 2019. A send to a listed address is accepted and counted against the quota but not attempted.

reasons.title: Reasons
reasons.description: Which outcomes put an address on the list. An address listed for another reason is mailed anyway. One of: both (Bounces and complaints), bounces (Bounces only), complaints (Complaints only).

reputation.title: Reputation
reputation.description: The review and pause AWS applies to accounts with a high bounce or complaint rate.

enforcement.title: Reputation enforcement
enforcement.description: SES reviews the account at 5% bounces or 0.1% complaints and may pause sending at 10% or 0.5% if the review ends unresolved. Turn off to ignore it.

window.title: Representative volume
window.description: The rates are measured over the last this-many recipients. AWS only says it uses a 'representative volume' that depends on the account; the size is an assumption. In recipients.

minVolume.title: Minimum volume
minVolume.description: Recipients that must be in the window before its rates can start a review or a pause: a handful of sends proves nothing. An assumption. In recipients.

reviewPeriod.title: Review period
reviewPeriod.description: How long an account under review has to fix the problem. AWS states the end date in its notification and publishes no length; an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

pauseDuration.title: Pause duration
pauseDuration.description: How long a pause lasts before AWS lifts it. In practice the owner opens a support case and AWS reviews it; the delay is an assumption. 0 keeps sending paused until enforcement is switched off. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

core.target-tracking.settings.description: Settings of Target tracking: only the ones you change.

metric.title: Metric
metric.description: What it watches on the target, as the target's metrics name it: a gauge (inflight, depth, concurrent), a rate per second (in, ok, fail), or a percentile such as latency.p95.

source.title: Metric of
source.description: Another node to read the metric from, by id: the queue whose backlog the target's workers drain (depth per instance, as Application Auto Scaling's backlog-per-instance policy does). Empty: the target's own.

per.title: Target is
per.description: Per unit: the target is per unit of the setting it changes (requests in flight per unit of concurrency, messages waiting per consumer), the way Kubernetes and Application Auto Scaling track. In total: the metric itself, and the setting moves in proportion. One of: unit (Per unit), total (In total).

targetValue.title: Target value
targetValue.description: The value it keeps the metric near.

setting.title: Setting it changes
setting.description: The number it scales on the target, as a path into the target's settings: provisioned, maxConcurrency, capacity.write.

window.title: Averaged over
window.description: The metric is averaged over this long before deciding. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

period.title: Decides every
period.description: Kubernetes' horizontal autoscaler looks every 15 seconds; Application Auto Scaling about once a minute. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

tolerance.title: Tolerance
tolerance.description: No change while the metric is within this fraction of the target. Kubernetes uses 10%. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

scaleOutCooldown.title: Scale-out cooldown
scaleOutCooldown.description: After a change, how long before it adds more. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

scaleInCooldown.title: Scale-in cooldown
scaleInCooldown.description: After a change, how long before it takes any away. Longer than scale-out, so a dip doesn't shed capacity a spike needs. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

type.description: What it is: common.client (Clients), common.http-endpoint (HTTP endpoint), common.service (Service), common.actor (Actors (keyed objects)), aws.region (Region), aws.vpc (VPC), aws.nat-gateway (NAT gateway), aws.vpc-endpoint (VPC endpoint), aws.apigateway (API Gateway), aws.cloudfront (CloudFront distribution), aws.route53 (Route 53 record), aws.waf (WAF web ACL), aws.alb (Application Load Balancer), aws.nlb (Network Load Balancer), aws.ec2 (EC2 Auto Scaling group), aws.ecs (ECS service), aws.eks (EKS workload), aws.lambda (Lambda function), aws.sqs (SQS queue), aws.sns (SNS topic), aws.kinesis (Kinesis data stream), aws.firehose (Firehose stream), aws.eventbridge (EventBridge event bus), aws.scheduler (EventBridge Scheduler), aws.stepfunctions (Step Functions state machine), aws.dynamodb (DynamoDB table), aws.rds (RDS database), aws.rds-proxy (RDS Proxy), aws.elasticache (ElastiCache cluster), aws.opensearch (OpenSearch domain), aws.s3 (S3 bucket), aws.ses (SES email).

name.description: What the canvas calls it. Defaults to its id.

region.description: The provider's region it runs in. Absent means the provider's default, or the region box it is in.

zone.description: The availability zone of its region it lives in (us-east-1a), for a single-zone resource: a zone outage takes it down. Absent for a regional one.

parent.description: The id of the container (a region or VPC box) it sits inside.

position.description: Where it sits on the canvas. Absent means it is laid out automatically.

size.description: A container's box size, in canvas units.

settings.description: Only the settings you change; the rest take the component's defaults.

origin.description: Where it came from when imported, so a re-import can find and merge it.

edge.description: A connection: calls or messages from one node's output to another node.

port.description: The output it leaves from, when the node has several (deliver, dlq, onFailure...). Default out.

connector.description: What sits on it. Absent means the most specific one that fits: core.link (Link), core.poller (Poller), core.target-group (Target group), aws.sqs.event-source-mapping (Event source mapping), aws.kinesis.event-source-mapping (Event source mapping (Kinesis)), aws.firehose.kinesis-source (Firehose source (Kinesis)), aws.route53.connection (Resolved connection), aws.stepfunctions.task (Task integration), aws.rds.client (Database client), aws.rds-proxy.client (Proxy client), aws.rds-proxy.target (Proxy connection pool), aws.alb.target-group (ALB target group), aws.alb.lambda-target (Lambda target), aws.alb.ip-target (IP target), aws.nlb.target-group (NLB target group), aws.nlb.ip-target (IP or ALB target).

settings.description: Only the settings you change: the port's, the connector's and transport's.

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: Share of traffic this edge gets when the source routes by weight.

operation.title: Operation
operation.description: What this call does to the receiver. Stores and object stores price and limit reads and writes differently. A hop that only passes calls on (a firewall, a load balancer, a cache in front of a store) keeps the caller's with "caller". One of: write (Write), read (Read), caller (What the caller asked (read or write)).

payload.title: Payload size
payload.description: Size of what this call carries. 0 keeps the size the sender gave it. In KB.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: How long the caller waits before giving up. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cancelOnTimeout.title: Cancel on timeout
cancelOnTimeout.description: Off: the callee keeps working after the caller gives up (wasted work, like most real clients). On: the work is cancelled.

backoff.title: Initial backoff
backoff.description: A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

maxBackoff.title: Max backoff
maxBackoff.description: A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

jitter.title: Jitter
jitter.description: Randomise each wait between zero and its full length.

workers.title: Workers
workers.description: How many take a batch and call with it at the same time. Each waits for its call before taking more. In workers.

batchSize.title: Batch size
batchSize.description: Records taken for one call, at most. In records.

backoff.title: Pause after a failure
backoff.description: How long a worker waits after a failed call before it takes again. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

algorithm.title: Algorithm
algorithm.description: How a target is picked for each request: in turn, the one with the fewest requests in flight from this balancer, at random, or by the request's key (one key always reaches the same target while the targets don't change). One of: round-robin (Round robin), least-outstanding (Least outstanding requests), random (Random), flow-hash (Flow hash (by key)).

crossZone.title: Cross-zone
crossZone.description: On: a request may go to a target in any zone. Off: only to targets in the zone where it reached the balancer, so a zone with fewer targets gives each of them more.

slowStart.title: Slow start
slowStart.description: A target that just became healthy gets a share of requests that grows linearly to a full one over this long. 0: off. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

deregistrationDelay.title: Deregistration delay
deregistrationDelay.description: How long a target the fleet lets go is kept to finish its requests (it gets no new ones). It goes sooner if it finishes them. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

failOpen.title: Fail open
failOpen.description: With no healthy target at all, send to every registered target anyway, as ALB and NLB do. Off: refuse (503).

replaceUnhealthy.title: Fleet replaces unhealthy targets
replaceUnhealthy.description: Tell the fleet when a target fails its health checks, so it replaces it: what an ECS service does, and an Auto Scaling group whose health check type is ELB.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Off: every registered target counts as healthy.

interval.title: Interval
interval.description: Time between checks of one target. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: A check with no answer in this long fails. Never longer than the interval. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

healthyThreshold.title: Healthy threshold
healthyThreshold.description: Passes in a row before an unhealthy target counts as healthy again. A newly registered one needs a single pass. In checks.

unhealthyThreshold.title: Unhealthy threshold
unhealthyThreshold.description: Failures in a row before a target counts as unhealthy. In checks.

batchWindow.title: Batching window
batchWindow.description: How long to wait for a batch to fill. Standard queues only. The messages are already received, so their visibility timeout is running while the batch fills: AWS advises a visibility timeout of six times the function timeout plus this window. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

maxConcurrency.title: Maximum concurrency
maxConcurrency.description: Cap on concurrent invocations from this queue. 0 for none (the mapping then scales up to 1,250). AWS accepts 2 to 1,000, and not together with provisioned mode. In invocations. A hard limit of the provider.

initialConcurrency.title: Starting concurrency
initialConcurrency.description: A standard queue's mapping starts with 5 concurrent batches. AWS fixes this at 5; it is editable here to explore what-ifs. In invocations. A hard limit of the provider.

scaleUpPerMinute.title: Scale-up rate
scaleUpPerMinute.description: Invocations added each minute while messages are waiting, up to 1,250. AWS publishes this for standard queues only; the same ramp is used for FIFO. In per minute. A hard limit of the provider.

reportBatchItemFailures.title: Report batch item failures
reportBatchItemFailures.description: FunctionResponseTypes: ReportBatchItemFailures. A function that returns the records that failed has only those come back after the visibility timeout; the rest are deleted. Off, such a reply is ignored: the invocation succeeded, so the whole batch is deleted, the failed records with it. A FIFO batch keeps a failed record's later messages of the same group too, as a correct FIFO handler reports them.

throttleRetry.title: Throttle retry
throttleRetry.description: When the function is throttled, the mapping keeps the batch and tries again after this long, until the queue's visibility timeout runs out. AWS says Lambda backs off and retries but publishes no interval: this is an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

provisionedMinPollers.title: Provisioned mode: minimum pollers
provisionedMinPollers.description: 0 leaves provisioned mode off. Otherwise (AWS accepts 2 to 200) the mapping starts with this many dedicated pollers, each driving up to 10 concurrent invocations, and adds up to 1,000 invocations a minute. Overrides maximum concurrency, as in AWS. In pollers. A hard limit of the provider.

provisionedMaxPollers.title: Provisioned mode: maximum pollers
provisionedMaxPollers.description: Upper bound on pollers in provisioned mode: 100,000 concurrent invocations at 10,000. The AWS pages disagree on this maximum (2,000 on the parameters page, 10,000 on the newer scaling pages); the newer figure is used. In pollers. A hard limit of the provider.

parallelization.title: Parallelization factor
parallelization.description: Batches processed from each shard at the same time. Records with the same partition key stay in order: a shard is split by key into this many lanes, so a hot key stays in one lane and gains nothing. A hard limit of the provider.

maxRecordAge.title: Maximum record age
maxRecordAge.description: A failing batch whose oldest record is older than this is discarded instead of retried. -1: retried until the stream's retention drops it, so one bad record blocks its shard that long. AWS refuses 0 to 59; they are read as 60. In s. A hard limit of the provider.

maxRetries.title: Maximum retry attempts
maxRetries.description: Retries of a batch the function failed before it is discarded. -1: until it expires. Throttling doesn't count: a throttled batch is retried until it is too old. A hard limit of the provider.

bisectOnError.title: Split batch on error
bisectOnError.description: BisectBatchOnFunctionError: a batch the function failed is split in two, the halves tried in order, until the bad record is alone. Splitting doesn't use up retries.

enhancedFanOut.title: Enhanced fan-out
enhancedFanOut.description: Read through a registered consumer: records are pushed (no polling) and this mapping gets its own 2 MiB/s per shard instead of sharing 2 MiB/s and five calls a second with every other standard reader. A stream can register 20.

retryBackoff.title: Retry backoff
retryBackoff.description: Wait before retrying a failed batch, doubling each time up to the cap. AWS doesn't publish the schedule: an assumption. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

maxRetryBackoff.title: Retry backoff cap
maxRetryBackoff.description: An assumption: AWS doesn't publish it. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

poisonRecords.title: Poison records
poisonRecords.description: Share of records this function can never process (bad data meeting this code). A batch holding one fails every time; with batch item failures on, the function reports it instead. A modelling device: the stream carries no record contents. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

connections.title: Connections
connections.description: Kept open: a connection pool, or a Lambda function that connects outside its handler (one connection per execution environment). It is opened (handshake and all) only when no idle one is free, and stays open, counting against max_connections, until it has been idle for the idle timeout. One per request: a function that connects inside its handler pays the handshake on every request. One of: reused (Kept open and reused), per-request (One per request).

idleTimeout.title: Idle timeout
idleTimeout.description: How long an idle connection stays open: a pool's idle timeout, or how long a Lambda execution environment lives idle (the connection goes with it). An assumption: pools and runtimes differ, and AWS doesn't publish Lambda's. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

hold.title: Held besides the query
hold.description: How long the caller keeps its connection checked out around each query, besides the query itself. A database sees only the query, but a Lambda function holds its connection for its whole invocation (its execution environment's one connection, or the one it opened in its handler), so set this to the function's duration besides the query; a service that borrows from its pool just for the query leaves it at 0. This, more than anything, decides how many connections a caller needs: about its request rate times the time it holds each. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.description: Which endpoint the client connects to. With no readers the reader endpoint reaches the writer. A write sent to a reader is refused. One of: auto (Reads to the readers, writes to the writer), writer (Writer (cluster endpoint)), reader (Readers (reader endpoint)).

dnsCache.title: DNS cache
dnsCache.description: How long the client caches the endpoint's address. A failover moves the endpoint's DNS name to the new primary, and a client still caching the old address keeps failing to connect until its cache expires. 0: it looks the name up every time. AWS advises a JVM to cache for no more than 60 seconds. A proxy isn't affected: it follows the primary itself. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

stickiness.title: Sticky sessions
stickiness.description: Send a client (a message key) back to the same target while it stays registered and healthy. Modelled as a hash of the key over the targets, so a change of targets moves some clients; the cookie's duration is not modelled. Not with cross-zone off or weighted random (AWS refuses both).

originType.title: Origin type
originType.description: An S3 bucket does not offer the origin response timeout: it is not retried on a slow response. A custom origin is retried on a timeout for GET and HEAD. One of: custom (Custom HTTP origin (ALB, EC2, API Gateway...)), s3 (S3 bucket).

role.title: Role
role.description: Primary origins split the objects by this edge's weight, like cache behaviours by path. A secondary origin is only called when a primary fails the failover criteria, and only for reads. One of: primary (Primary (or an origin on its own)), secondary (Secondary (origin group failover)).

shield.title: Origin Shield
shield.description: Put Origin Shield in front of this origin: one more cache layer that collapses requests from every regional cache into one.

connectionAttempts.title: Connection attempts
connectionAttempts.description: How many times CloudFront tries a refused connection (and, for a custom origin, an origin that does not answer) before giving up or failing over. A hard limit of the provider.

responseTimeout.title: Response timeout
responseTimeout.description: How long CloudFront waits for the origin to answer before it drops the connection (a 504 once the attempts are used). Applies to custom origins. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

responseCompletionTimeout.title: Response completion timeout
responseCompletionTimeout.description: The longest CloudFront waits for the whole origin response across every attempt. 0 for no limit. When set it must be at least the response timeout. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

location.title: Location
location.description: Geolocation routing: the continent this record answers. Without a default record, callers from anywhere else get no answer. One of: default (Default (everywhere else)), AF (Africa), AN (Antarctica), AS (Asia), EU (Europe), NA (North America), OC (Oceania), SA (South America).

filterMatch.title: Filter policy match rate
filterMatch.description: The share of messages this subscription's filter policy lets through; the rest are filtered out and never delivered. 1 means no filter policy. Simulated messages carry no attributes or body to match, so this is a rate, not a rule. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

rawMessageDelivery.title: Raw message delivery
rawMessageDelivery.description: On: the subscriber gets exactly what was published. Off: SNS wraps it in a JSON envelope of about 1024 bytes (an assumption). AWS's own default is off; the simulator defaults to on so a design's message sizes are unchanged.

deadLetterQueue.title: Dead-letter queue
deadLetterQueue.description: When delivery finally fails (retries used up, or the endpoint refuses the message), send the message to the queue wired to this topic's dead-letter port instead of discarding it. The redrive policy of the subscription.

maxReceivesPerSecond.title: Delivery throttle
maxReceivesPerSecond.description: The throttle policy of an HTTP/S delivery policy (maxReceivesPerSecond): SNS holds deliveries back to this average rate per subscription, and held messages do not use up retries. 0 for no throttle. In msg/s.

rule.title: Rule
rule.description: The rule this target belongs to. Edges that name the same rule are its targets (up to 5): an event the rule matches goes to all of them. Empty: the edge is a rule of its own.

match.title: Event pattern match rate
match.description: The share of events the rule's event pattern matches. Simulated events carry no fields to match, so this is a rate, not a pattern. Targets of one rule draw together: with the same rate they all receive the same events. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

maxRetries.title: Maximum retries
maxRetries.description: Retries after the first attempt (MaximumRetryAttempts). 0 tries once. A hard limit of the provider.

maxEventAge.title: Maximum event age
maxEventAge.description: Stop retrying once the event is this old (MaximumEventAgeInSeconds), counted from when it was accepted. Time spent delayed by a rate limit counts too. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

enabled.title: API destination
enabled.description: The target is an HTTPS endpoint called through an API destination: each request is given 5 seconds, and invocations are held to the destination's rate.

rate.title: Invocation rate limit
rate.description: InvocationRateLimitPerSecond. Invocations beyond it are delayed, not refused, and can outlive their maximum event age. In req/s. The provider's default quota; it can be raised.

state.title: State type
state.description: Task calls what this edge leads to once with the execution's input. Map calls it once for each item of the input (the message's records), several at a time. One of: task (Task), map (Map: a task per item).

parallel.title: Parallel with the state before
parallel.description: This state and the one wired before it run at once, as branches of one Parallel state, which waits for all of them; the first to fail stops it. A run of states with this on are all branches of the same Parallel state.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Inline: iterations run inside this execution, at most 40 at once, and their events fill its history. Distributed: each item is a child workflow execution with a history of its own, up to 10,000 at once. Express workflows can't use Distributed mode; there it runs as Inline. One of: inline (Inline), distributed (Distributed).

items.title: Items
items.description: How many items the Map iterates over (the array its ItemsPath selects). 0 takes the input's records: a batch from a queue is many, a client's request is one. Simulated inputs carry no arrays, so set a number to stand for the one in the input. The upper bound is this form's. In items.

maxConcurrency.title: MaxConcurrency
maxConcurrency.description: Iterations at once. 0 places no limit of its own: Inline mode still runs at most 40, Distributed 10,000. Lower it to stay inside what the task (a Lambda function's concurrency) can take. In iterations. A hard limit of the provider.

childType.title: Child executions
childType.description: Distributed mode only: the type of each child workflow execution (ExecutionType). Express children start at up to 1,000 a second and use no state transition quota; Standard ones at up to 100 a second, and their transitions are throttled like the parent's. One of: express (Express), standard (Standard).

toleratedFailure.title: ToleratedFailurePercentage
toleratedFailure.description: Distributed mode only: the share of items that may fail before the Map Run fails. 0 fails it on the first failed item; 100% never does. Inline mode fails on the first failed iteration. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

wait.title: Wait before (Wait state)
wait.description: A Wait state that runs just before this one: a state transition, then a pause of this long. 0 for none. A Standard workflow can wait up to a year, an Express one five minutes (the execution's own limit). A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Give this state a Retry field. Without one, Step Functions doesn't retry a failed state: the error goes to the catcher, or fails the execution. Each retry is a state transition, throttled like one.

errorEquals.title: ErrorEquals
errorEquals.description: Which errors this retrier retries; any other goes straight to the catcher. AWS recommends retrying Lambda's service errors and throttling on every Lambda task. One of: States.ALL (States.ALL (every error)), States.TaskFailed (States.TaskFailed (all but States.Timeout)), States.Timeout (States.Timeout (TimeoutSeconds ran out)), service (Service errors and throttling (Lambda.ServiceException, Lambda.TooManyRequestsException...)), throttling (Throttling only (Lambda.TooManyRequestsException...)), function (The task's own error (Lambda.Unknown, Sandbox.Timedout, a custom error)).

interval.title: IntervalSeconds
interval.description: Wait before the first retry. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

maxAttempts.title: MaxAttempts
maxAttempts.description: Retries after the first try (so 3 means up to four tries). 0 never retries. In retries. A hard limit of the provider.

backoffRate.title: BackoffRate
backoffRate.description: Each wait is the one before times this. A hard limit of the provider.

maxDelay.title: MaxDelaySeconds
maxDelay.description: The longest a wait may grow to. 0 means no MaxDelaySeconds: the waits grow without limit. A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes". A hard limit of the provider.

jitter.title: JitterStrategy
jitter.description: FULL draws each wait at random between zero and its full length, so executions that failed together don't retry together. AWS's default is NONE. One of: NONE (None), FULL (Full).

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Give this state a Catch field: an error its retrier didn't resolve sends the execution down the fallback path (the states wired to the `catch` port) instead of failing it.

errorEquals.title: ErrorEquals
errorEquals.description: Which errors are caught. Any other fails the execution. One of: States.ALL (States.ALL (every error)), States.TaskFailed (States.TaskFailed (all but States.Timeout)), States.Timeout (States.Timeout (TimeoutSeconds ran out)), service (Service errors and throttling (Lambda.ServiceException, Lambda.TooManyRequestsException...)), throttling (Throttling only (Lambda.TooManyRequestsException...)), function (The task's own error (Lambda.Unknown, Sandbox.Timedout, a custom error)).

undoes.title: Compensates
undoes.description: The state this one undoes, by the id of the node its `out` edge leads to: it runs only if the execution had reached that state when it failed (the failing state included, since it may have half happened). Empty, or an id no state of this workflow leads to, runs it whatever failed. Wire the compensations in the order they should run, usually the reverse of the states they undo.

eventTypes.title: Event types
eventTypes.description: Which changes this destination is subscribed to: s3:ObjectCreated:* (PUT, COPY, completed multipart upload), s3:ObjectRemoved:* (DELETE), or both. One of: all (Created and removed), created (Object created), removed (Object removed).

filter.title: Share matching the filter
filter.description: A notification can be filtered by key prefix and suffix. The simulator has no key names, so a filter is the fraction of matching events that it lets through: 1 is no filter, 0.1 is a filter that matches one object in ten. A fraction: 0.25 is 25%.

events.title: Event types
events.description: The matching event types of this event destination.

send.title: Send
send.description: SES accepted the message and will try to deliver it (also counted when delivery is then suppressed).

delivery.title: Delivery
delivery.description: The recipient's mail server accepted the message.

bounce.title: Bounce
bounce.description: A hard bounce, or a soft bounce SES has stopped retrying, or a send to a suppressed address.

complaint.title: Complaint
complaint.description: The recipient marked the message as spam.

reject.title: Reject
reject.description: SES accepted the message, found a virus in it and did not send it.

deliveryDelay.title: Delivery delay
deliveryDelay.description: A temporary problem delayed delivery; SES keeps retrying.

open.title: Open
open.description: The recipient opened the message (needs open tracking).

click.title: Click
click.description: The recipient clicked a link (needs click tracking).

latency.title: Network latency
latency.description: One-way; paid on the way there and back. Unless set, it is estimated from where the two nodes run.

mean.title: Average
mean.description: Typical time taken A duration: a number of milliseconds, or text such as "30 seconds" or "2 minutes".

cv.title: Variability
cv.description: Coefficient of variation: 0 is constant, 1 is heavily spread

origin.description: Where it came from when imported, so a re-import can find and merge it.

controller.description: A loop that watches a node and changes it while the design runs, such as an autoscaler.

target.description: The id of the node it changes.

scenario.description: What happens to this design: a timeline of faults and changes, and the checks that must hold.

description.description: What it shows. The first paragraph is its short blurb.

seed.description: Random seed for the run: the same design, scenario and seed always play out the same.

duration.description: How long to run. Required to run it.

warmup.description: Time to let the system settle before measuring: checks and summaries start after it.

scale.description: Multiply every client's request rate: 3 is three times the traffic.

overrides.description: Settings applied at the start, merged over the design's own.

timeline.description: What happens, and when. Each event does one thing; an event with only a note annotates the timeline.

at.description: When it happens, from the start of the run.

note.description: Says what this event is, in the timeline.

target.description: What breaks: node:<id>, edge:<id>, region:<placement> (region:aws:us-east-1) or zone:<placement>:<zone> (zone:aws:us-east-1:us-east-1a).

fault.description: The fault: Outage (Rejects every call at once, like a connection refused or a stopped service. On a region, the whole region is down; on a zone, everything placed in it and every unit a fleet runs there.) Errors (A fraction of calls fail with a server error after being processed.) Slow (Adds fixed latency to every call.) Blackhole (Calls vanish without a reply; callers wait out their full timeout.) Loss (A fraction of calls vanish without a reply.) Crash (Crashes some of a fleet's units at once (EC2 instances, ECS tasks, EKS pods or nodes): calls on them fail, a load balancer keeps sending them traffic until its health checks catch them, and the fleet replaces them when it notices. It happens in an instant; on a component that isn't a fleet it does nothing.) Write it as Outage, Slow(250ms), Errors(20%), Loss(10%), or as an object { type: Slow, extra: 250ms }.

extra.description: A time: a number of seconds, or text such as 90s, 2m, 1h30m, 250ms or "2 minutes".

for.description: How long it lasts. Without it, the fault lasts until cleared.

id.description: A name to clear it by later.

clear.description: Lift a fault by the id it was injected with, or all of them (all).

set.description: Change a node's or an edge's settings while it runs.

settings.description: Settings, merged over what it already has.

account.description: Change the account quotas of a placement while it runs.

settings.description: Settings, merged over what it already has.

assert.description: What must hold. A run passes when every check does.

anyOf.description:
A check that must hold over the run (after the warm-up unless a window is given), in the check language:

<subject>.<metric>[:<aggregate>] <op> <value> [@ <from>..<to>]

subject   a node id; edge:<edge id>; or system (every client together)
metric    errorRatio | successRatio | throughput
          rate.<counter>          per-second rate of a counter: rate.ok, rate.fail, rate.fail.Throttled, rate.in, rate.sent
          total.<counter>         how many events in the window
          gauge.<name>            a gauge: gauge.depth, gauge.concurrent, gauge.inflight, gauge.cacheHitRate
          latency.<stat>          p50 | p95 | p99 | mean | max, of the 'latency' distribution (other distributions: dist.<name>.<stat>)
aggregate how to combine the window's frames: mean (default) | max | min | last | sum
op        < <= > >= == !=
value     a number, with optional unit: 500ms, 2s, 1.5%, 10/s
window    @ 2m..3m measures only that stretch (default: after the warm-up, to the end of the run)

examples  api.errorRatio < 1%
          system.latency.p99 < 800ms
          orders-queue.gauge.depth:max < 5000
          fn.rate.fail.Throttled == 0
          edge:web.out->api.rate.fail < 5/s @ 4m..6m

op        < <= > >= == !=
value     a number, with optional unit: 500ms, 2s, 1.5%, 10/s

from.description: Measure only from here (default: the end of the warm-up).

to.description: ... to here (default: the end of the run).
